articles.title: Steelers and Broncos players sending Aaron Rodgers signs through their scoring play celebrations
articles.excerpt: Barstool College Football Show co-host Kayce Smith breaks down the escalating feud between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after Rodgers criticized the coach following ...
articles.body_text:
Barstool College Football Show co-host Kayce Smith breaks down the escalating feud between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after Rodgers criticized the coach following his benching and release. Smith also reacts to Crunch Fitness testing dedicated influencer filming zones in Arizona and Florida.

After much was made of Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers this week, an actual game began between the quarterback's former team and the Denver Broncos on Friday.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

And players from both teams made their scores about, you guessed it, Aaron Rodgers.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers talks to wide receiver DK Metcalf during pregame before a preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Aug. 16, 2025, at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pa. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

The Steelers took a surprising 14-0 lead in the first quarter, with the second of their scores coming on a 22-yard pass from new starting quarterback Mason Rudolph to DK Metcalf.

AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS

And after the score, Metcalf made a couple of hand signals as his celebration. One of those was Metcalf holding up four fingers on each hand.

Several people on social media who apparently read sign language translated Metcalf's sign language to mean: "Stand on business, 8."

In the second quarter, the Broncos scored their first points of the game when Alex Singleton tackled Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety.

And immediately Singleton started celebrating with an old-school Rodgers "Discount Double Check" celebration from maybe 15 years ago.

Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) calls signals behind center during the first half of an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Cincinnati, Thursday, Oct. 16, 2025. (AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster)

MIKE TOMLIN CALLS STEELERS SITUATION FOLLOWING AARON RODGERS VS. MIKE MCCARTHY FEUD 'A DUMPSTER FIRE'

Rodgers is gone from the Steelers. He sealed his fate this week when he went scorched-earth on Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.

That has become the biggest story around the NFL this week. It's clear players in the Steelers locker room, such as Metcalf, are not going to soon forget their former leader.

The Steelers, by the way, scored another touchdown when Jalen Ramsey returned a Bo Nix interception for a touchdown. Amazon Prime cameras cut to the crowd and sideline reaction rather than focusing on Ramsey after the score, so we don't know if he signaled on behalf of Rodgers, but it didn't seem so.

Things got heated during a Denver Broncos practice on Tuesday and quarterback Bo Nix was right in the middle of it. (Photo by RJ Sangosti/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images)

It is nonetheless wild that some Broncos players saw what happened Wednesday while they were on a short week of preparation, traveled across the country on Thanksgiving and still had time to come up with a celebration that spoke to the big story.

There's only one way to respond to this: Cheer for more reasons for celebration to see if Aaron Rodgers continues to haunt this game.

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
articles.excerpt:
Pedro Sánchez accused his opponents of hurling insults and lies but his conservative rival has promised a new era of politics

Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday'...
articles.body_text:
Pedro Sánchez accused his opponents of hurling insults and lies but his conservative rival has promised a new era of politics

Spain's main party leaders have held their final rallies ahead of Sunday's election, with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez saying he is confident of defying the polls.

"I cannot imagine us losing," he said, posing for selfies with supporters in red T-shirts and accusing conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo of planning a coalition with the far right.

Feijóo's People's Party (PP) is narrowly ahead in the polls, and in the final hours of the campaign he travelled first to Barcelona and then Seville, promising voters a new political era of "truth, decency and good governance".

He accused Sánchez of evading questions on key issues like corruption, rail disasters, immigration and the national debt.

Alberto Núñez Feijóo's PP holds a narrow lead in the opinion polls

The Socialist leader heads one of Europe's few left-wing governments, and with the French presidential elections five months away, there is a real chance that two of the continent's biggest economies could move to the right in quick succession.

Almost 39 million people have a vote in Spain and while commentators expect a high turnout, most polls have suggested a close finish. Under Spanish electoral law, no polls have been published since Monday.

"This time, yes, we're going to do it," Feijóo told PP supporters, in a nod to his failure to form a government three years ago despite winning most seats.

Abascal said on Friday that Sánchez's government had 'betrayed' Spaniards

If he gets to form a government this time, it will be with the support of anti-immigration party Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, whose final rally took place in front of thousands of people in a bull-ring in Valencia on Spain's east coast.

The venue was filled with Spanish flags and green Vox banners, and one of the biggest cheers of the night came when the secretary general of the party called for "less burka and less halal".

Ignacio Garriga said he was not acting out of hatred but love for the homeland.

A small section of the crowd could be heard chanting "Viva Franco" in reference to the dictator, whose death in 1975 heralded the start of Spain's transition to democracy.

A number of first-time voters at the rally said they were supporting Vox because of its policies on immigration.

Lledó, 18, said what had happened in Ceuta in the summer, when more than 70,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish territory from Morocco, showed Sánchez was not able to control the country's border.

She had come to the bullring with her mum and aunt, Carli Chilet, who argued that Vox "are the best for women's rights".

Vox is hoping to almost double its seats from the 33 it won three years ago. It backs policies such as "national priority" - putting Spanish citizens first for welfare - and "remigration" for foreigners not considered to be contributing to the economy.

Leaders clash in final Spain election debate as housing dominates run-in

Spanish election: What you need to know and what's at stake

Clashing political visions reflect a divided Spain ahead of election

The final day of campaigning was very much in the shadow of a four-way TV debate the night before that exposed Spain's sharply polarised politics.

All four leaders had solutions for the housing crisis. Feijóo said the PP would build a million homes over four years, while Sánchez said housing should be a right not an object of speculation and profit.

Watch: Could housing decide Spain's general election?

While the conservatives tried to turn the spotlight on the series of scandals that have overshadowed the Socialists' term in office, Sánchez and his left-wing ally Ada Colau, who heads Frente Amplio (The Broad Front), focused on women's rights.

The two leaders seized on a moment in the debate when the PP leader accused Colau and the rest of the left of staying quiet during a flood disaster in Valencia, briefly moving his finger to his lips. The word he used "calladita" is a diminutive and can also be used to tell a woman to "keep quiet" in a condescending manner.

Sánchez reacted immediately and called on him to show "a little respect", accusing him of sexism.

Feijóo sought to clarify what he meant on Friday, and accused Ada Colau of remaining silent during "these years of corruption". His decision to wind up his campaign in Seville was significant, because the wider southern region of Andalusia has 61 seats in Spain's 350-seat parliament, more than any other.

Andalusia is also important because it is run by a coalition made up of the PP and Abascal's Vox, as are three other regions, Extremadura, Aragón, and Castilla y León.

Feijóo has insisted he wants to govern with a majority, backed up by "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox and says he has never spoken to Abascal about giving Vox ministerial power.

"Governing is about managing, and I have spent my whole life preparing for this moment," he said in Seville.

One of his new supporters at the rally was a retired woman called Isabel who told Spanish public broadvaster RTVE that she was attending a PP rally for the first time. The formerly loyal Socialist voter said she was "disillusioned" with a party led by  Sánchez. Another voter at the rally said Spain needed "a good manager".

Sánchez took to the stage in Madrid with his wife Begoña Gómez, and donned a red T-shirt that read "power of the people".

He then went on to praise Colau and her left-wing coalition's campaign.

"These elections are about moving Spain forward, not taking it backwards," he said.

Socialist supporter Leon Felipe, 25, told Reuters news agency: "Well, I think what's at stake in these elections is a big deal, is not a change of government... but rather a return to the past - a return to Franco's dictatorship.

"So, I believe that young must mobilise."

As he was speaking, Colau told a large audience in the south of Madrid that not only would they "not remain silent, we will win", vowing to form another "progressive government".

articles.title: New California law could keep teens in booster seats until age 16 unless they pass test
articles.excerpt:
Why buckling a child into a car seat with heavy winter layers is not recommended.

Beginning in the new year, minors will be required to pass a five-step seat belt fit test before they can ride withou...
articles.body_text:
Why buckling a child into a car seat with heavy winter layers is not recommended.

Beginning in the new year, minors will be required to pass a five-step seat belt fit test before they can ride without a booster seat or sit in the front seat of a vehicle. The bill's author, Assemblymember Lori Wilson, cited figures showing that child injuries and fatalities in crashes have risen since the pandemic, with children ages 8 to 12 disproportionately affected.

"Extending the required age for booster use and implementing straightforward testing can significantly enhance child safety," CalMatters reported.

"So the best thing to do to keep your child safe while riding in a vehicle matches what our law is," Wilson said of the bill in April 2025. "It really is to take into consideration all the varying types of seats that we sit on in the car. This is about safety.

"This is about making sure that if something happens, you are safe, and I think that’s the key thing that we’re trying to drive home is that it is not about treating people like babies."

3 CAR SEAT INSTALLATION MISTAKES YOU NEED TO AVOID

A California law could keep children, including some teenagers, in booster seats until age 16.  (Cars.com)

Previously, children ages 8 and older — or those at least 4 feet, 9 inches tall — could ride without a booster seat. Under the new law, Assembly Bill 435, children ages 8 to 15 may use a regular seat belt without a booster only if they meet all five criteria:

MELATONIN WARNINGS: NEARLY HALF OF PARENTS GIVE IT TO THEIR KIDS TO HELP THEM SLEEP, BUT EXPERTS URGE CAUTION

Side shot on the seats for children mounted in minivan. A new law in Italy requires child car seats to be equipped with alarm devices to prevent parents from leaving children inside vehicles for hours.  (iStock)

Improper car seat and booster use remains widespread, according to federal and industry studies.

A 2011 National Child Restraint Use Special Study found that 46% of car seats and booster seats had at least one major installation or use error that could reduce their effectiveness in a crash.

Nearly all seats had some form of misuse, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

A 2021 study by AAA and the National Safety Council found that more than half of all car seats brought to child passenger safety technicians for inspection were improperly installed or used, and that only one in five parents and caregivers sought expert help securing their child's seat.

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Liberal media and fans want Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker to fail because he's a Catholic conservative
articles.excerpt: Adam Vinatieri, the Pro Football Hall of Fame kicker who owns numerous NFL records, gave his take to OutKick on the Kansas City Chiefs' kicking situation as Harrison Butker continues to struggle with ...
articles.body_text:
Adam Vinatieri, the Pro Football Hall of Fame kicker who owns numerous NFL records, gave his take to OutKick on the Kansas City Chiefs' kicking situation as Harrison Butker continues to struggle with Justin Tucker waiting.

Few NFL players have drawn as much personal disdain from the political left as Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker.

The outspoken Catholic conservative has become a target for liberal sports fans and media personalities since delivering his 2024 commencement address at Benedictine College. His public support for Donald Trump, the Republican Party, campaigning with Senator Josh Hawley, and advocacy for traditional family values have only intensified that criticism.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Butker has been branded a misogynist for expressing the belief that motherhood is more fulfilling for women than climbing the corporate ladder. A stance that clearly aligns with his Catholic faith and those that attend Benedictine College, a Catholic college, which he was speaking too directly.

Since then, as we have seen from some of his most vocal critics, watching Butker miss field goals over the years, especially this season, appears to provide a sense of political vindication.

Unfortunately, the three-time Super Bowl champion has given those critics plenty of ammunition this season from media and fans.

Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker reacts after missing a field goal attempt during the first half of an NFL game against the Seattle Seahawks in Seattle on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson)

WIFE OF PATRICK MAHOMES UNLEASHES FIRE AND FURY TOWARDS REFS AFTER BOTCHED CALL IN BUFFALO

Many media members are still taking shots at Butker for his comments in the commencement speech years later.

On Pablo Torre's Thanksgiving episode, he invited ESPN's Mina Kimes and the clip shared on X had a caption that said, "Harrison Butker may not like our Thanksgiving episode." The clip featured a male cook preparing some Thanksgiving dishes. Mina Kimes, still clearly triggered by Butker said, "How triggered do you think Harrison Butker would be if he turned this on and saw a bunch of men cooking for me?"

MINA KIMES CRACKS HARRISON BUTKER JOKE ABOUT MEN IN THE KITCHEN WITH CALLBACK TO KICKER'S COMMENCEMENT SPEECH

After the Chiefs worst game of the season on Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks, also being Butker's worst game of the season, going 1-for-3 on field goals, Nick Wright took a political shot at Butker.

"He started splitting his time between football and activism, and he hasn't been quite as good. That is just the timeline of it," Wright said.

There's clearly a political bias here and even making this topic political is unprofessional, in my opinion.

Also, Butker didn't immediately regress after becoming more politically outspoken. In fact, he converted every field goal and extra point he attempted between campaigning with Senator Josh Hawley during the Chiefs bye week in 2024 and suffering his knee injury. Maybe Wright should've spoken about how the knee injury and becoming the NFL's highest paid kicker could have effected Butker's performance.

On Thanksgiving fans took plenty of shots at Butker after missing a crucial 46-yard field goal with the game tied against the Buffalo Bills.

Denver news anchor Kyle Clark posted on X, "Butker. Wide right. Happy Thanksgiving, America." He later responded to a comment about rooting for and against players based on political party affiliation, Clark said, "Hi anonymous friend. Happy to clear this up for you. Whether my wife and my daughters should be able to have a job is not politics. It’s human rights. Have a Happy Thanksgiving!"

Again, a false retelling of what Butker said and believes.

Former Minnesota Star Tribune journalist Jim Souhan said, "Someone said that Butker’s pronouns are Miss/Misses and I’ll never forget it."

Editor-in Chief at radically liberal news outlet Meidas Touch, Ron Filipkowski took a shot as well by sharing a photo of Butker with President Trump on top of a post from an Associated Press reporter that stated, "Harrison Butker is tied with Trey Smack for most missed kicks this season with 9 (8 FGs, 1 PAT) and his 24 missed kicks (17 FGs, 7 PATs) since start of 2024 are most in NFL."

Obviously, when Butker misses to the right, the jokes write themselves, so those don't bother me. It's the low-hanging fruit that is easy to pick.

What we do need to discuss is how bad Butker has been statistically can be somewhat misleading.

Kansas City Chiefs place kicker Harrison Butker celebrates after scoring against the Los Angeles Rams during the first half of an NFL preseason football game, Saturday, Aug. 15, 2026, in Kansas City, Mo. (AP)

In August 2024, 86 days after his controversial commencement speech at Benedictine College, the Kansas City Chiefs rewarded Butker with a four-year, $25.6 million contract extension, making him the highest-paid kicker in NFL history at the time. Whether you're right, left, or center, you could agree at that time, Butker deserved this. The Chiefs clearly did not care that liberals were calling for Butker to be cut from the team for his comments on traditional roles within the household.

Butker was coming off a 2023 campaign in which he converted 33 of his 35 field goal attempts and made every extra point. He also drilled a Super Bowl-record 57-yard field goal against the San Francisco 49ers. He was arguably the Super Bowl MVP for much of the game.

Unfortunately, his field goal percentage has declined every season since signing that lucrative extension.

Butker currently owns the worst field goal percentage among NFL kickers with at least 15 attempts this season. However, a closer examination of his numbers reveals that his struggles are overwhelmingly concentrated in one area: long-distance field goals.

According to NFL.com, Butker has converted just two of his eight attempts from 50-plus yards this season (25%). From inside 50 yards, he's 13-of-15 (86.7%), including a perfect 7-of-7 from inside 40 yards.

It's particulary shocking to see how bad he's been from distance because he hit a 69-yard field goal in preseason, which most likely would've been good from almost 80 yards.

HARRISON BUTKER'S 69-YARD FIELD GOAL DEMONSTRATES THE NFL'S LATEST BIG SCORING CONTROVERSY

Butker isn't the only highly compensated kicker struggling from deep, either.

Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey, who surpassed Butker as the highest-paid kicker in NFL history after signing a four-year, $28 million extension in April, is also experiencing the worst season of his career.

Aubrey has converted just six of his 11 attempts from 50-plus yards (54.5%) and is shooting a career-low 77.8% overall. He also missed a 40-yard field goal on Thanksgiving in Dallas' one-point loss to Philadelphia. That kick has been heavily debated online, with former Colts punter and placeholder Pat McAfee giving Aubrey grace because the laces were facing toward Aubrey.

Speaking about Aubrey's stats are not an excuse for Butker's poor performance, but it does provide some much-needed perspective. Clearly his struggles are not as scrutinized as Butker's, though he's paid more.

Kansas City Chiefs place kicker Harrison Butker (7) gets ready to kick an extra point during the second half against the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo., on Nov. 8, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

There is a difference between rooting for someone to fail because of their religious and political beliefs and legitimately criticizing their professional performance.

If you know me at all, I am not a LeBron James fan. Yes, his politics come into play in my dislike of him, but claiming poor play is because of campaigning for Hilary Clinton or Kamala Harris by me would hopefully cause many to scold me for refusing to provide proper sports analysis and instead, going for a political cheapshot.

In all honestly, I'd love nothing more than to see Butker return to being one of the most reliable kickers in football. But defending his right to express his Catholic faith and conservative values doesn't require defending his inability to consistently put a football through the uprights, especially from long distance.

The Chiefs are paying him elite money to deliver elite results, particularly in high-pressure situations with championship aspirations on the line. He has no one to blame but himself. He needs to be better.

Butker doesn't need to apologize for his faith, his political affiliations or his appreciation for traditional family values. He just needs to start making kicks again.

Until he does that, his critics, in and out of the media, will continue to tee off on who they consider to be their political enemy.

Jon is a writer and content creator for OutKick

articles.title: France kicks off defense-industry pact to build up counter-drone efforts
articles.excerpt: PARIS — France kicked off an initiative with its defense industry to produce counter-drone systems, a new chapter in efforts to foster a local drone ecosystem through “pacts” with industry that bring ...
articles.body_text:
PARIS — France kicked off an initiative with its defense industry to produce counter-drone systems, a new chapter in efforts to foster a local drone ecosystem through “pacts” with industry that bring together firms and military end users, cut procurement red tape and focus on fast contract delivery.

The new pact adds a counter-drone dimension to France’s existing drone pact and will run to the end of summer 2027, said Emmanuel Levacher, chairman of defense-industry association Gicat and the CEO of military vehicle maker Arquus.

“We then hope it will be renewed while incorporating both drone and counter-drone, the idea being that one does not go without the other,” Levacher told Defense News on Wednesday night, after a presentation of the new counter-drone pact in the offices of semiconductor maker STMicroelectronics, just outside Paris.

The drone pact announced in June 2024 has been an attempt by France to play catch up in tactical drones and loitering munitions, led by the country’s Directorate General for Armament together with Gicat. Following up on the success of the original drone pact, France in November announced a similar pact for naval drones, on the occasion of the Euronaval defense trade show.

The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have been a “quite brutal reality check,” and French forces have an urgent need for counter-drone capabilities, Alice Rufo, France’s junior minister for the armed forces, said in a speech at the presentation. She said France has already faced problems related to having insufficient counter-drone capability, without providing details.

France has faced multiple incidents with drones overflying sensitive military sites, including the Île Longue nuclear submarine base in December 2025 and the Toulon naval base in October this year. French media have also reported drones flying over a Eurenco explosives plant in Bergerac and a freight train carrying Leclerc main battle tanks near Mulhouse in November 2025.

The new pact covers systems to counter unmanned aerial vehicles but also maritime and ground drones, according to Levacher. The Gicat chairman said he expects most or all of the 200 partners in the drone pact to participate in the counter-drone initiative.

The goal of the counter-drone pact is “to really be in contact with the armed forces” to understand their requirements, as well as with the DGA to facilitate testing, validation and orders, Levacher said.

“The idea is really to bring together all the stakeholders to create this cross-pollination, speed, contacts,” Levacher said. “This pact is a way of saying that this is an area that does still need to structure and organize itself a little.”

The drone pact has functioned as a meeting place for industry where companies have been able to find project partners, as well as a forum to share feedback from Ukraine, according to Levacher. The DGA uses the drone pact as a framework for informal calls for ideas.

While the demand, the connections and the ecosystem are primarily French, the drone pact firms also pursue export opportunities, Levacher said.

Within the framework of the drone pact, French startup Harmattan AI won a contract in June 2025 to supply the French Army with 1,000 low-cost drones, which it delivered in January this year ahead of the Orion exercise.

Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.

articles.title: Saudi strike kills ’11 civilians’ in Yemen’s Taiz: Houthi media
articles.excerpt:

The attack reported on Friday hit the city of al-Turbah, locate...
articles.body_text:
Saudi air strikes have killed 11 civilians in Yemen’s Taiz governorate, according to news media affiliated with the Houthi armed group.

The attack reported on Friday hit the city of al-Turbah, located south of the provincial capital, Taiz.

The alleged strike comes as hostilities in Yemen continue between the Iran-backed rebel Houthi group and government forces backed by Saudi Arabia.

A local source said that a residential building was struck and that “most” of the victims were children, according to the media report.

Rescue teams retrieved eight bodies from the site, the report said. Three people remain missing beneath the rubble.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the reports. The Saudi Arabia-led coalition supporting the internationally-recognised Yemen government did not immediately comment.

The coalition said later on Friday that it had destroyed a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region.

Yemen has been racked by violence since the Iran-backed Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and other parts of the country in 2014, prompting Saudi Arabia to lead a military coalition in support of the internationally recognised government in March 2015.

Fighting between Yemeni government forces and the Houthis resumed in July, as the United States’ war on Iran escalated hostilities and the collapse of a 2022 ceasefire.

Some 13,343 people have been killed or injured since August, according to the World Health Organization, while the country is sliding into a humanitarian crisis.

The Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme said on Friday that Yemen is among conflict hotspots that face severe food insecurity.

The Norwegian Refugee Council warned this week that the renewed fighting has displaced thousands and piled pressure onto dangerously underfunded aid efforts.

Aid from the US, Germany and others has shrunk considerably in recent years, the nongovernmental organisation noted, saying it has received only 12 percent of funding for emergency shelter support in Yemen so far this year.

“Fighting has again displaced entire communities, while disrupted supply routes have driven up food and fuel prices,” NRC Secretary-General Jan Egeland said, warning that families across Yemen are being pushed deeper into need.

“All parties to the conflict bear responsibility for the vast scale of harm here,” Egeland stated.

Calling for better humanitarian access and civilian protection, he demanded that “the powerful countries backing the armed actors must commit to making this a reality”.

articles.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power after storms hit US on Thanksgiving
articles.excerpt:
Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits the US

Hundreds of thousands of people are without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Than...
articles.body_text:
Watch: Roofs torn off and streets under water as severe weather hits the US

Hundreds of thousands of people are without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

Eastern areas were lashed on Thursday by a powerful storm which brought high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. Pennsylvania remained the state worst hit by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring site Poweroutage.us.

Conditions are now expected to improve, though forecasters caution that it will take some time. The West Coast has also been affected by its own storms.

Flight disruption also persists, with hundreds more delays and cancellations reported on Friday - which is expected to be another busy travel day.

More than 2,500 flights within, into or out of the US were delayed on Thursday, and more than 450 were cancelled, according to Flightaware.com.

One passenger told the BBC he had been stuck at New York's LaGuardia Airport for 13 hours while trying to fly to see friends in Chicago for Thanksgiving.

Beyond the travel disruption, impacts were widespread across the East Coast, and US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds.

Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds, while waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.

On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport.

Parts of some states are under states of emergency, including New York.

Nearly 2in (5cm) of rain fail on New York City's iconic Central Park, making it the wettest Thanksgiving on record at that site as well, according to preliminary data, external from the NWS.

Organisers of the city's annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have also pushed back the event to Saturday - marking the event's first postponement 100-year history.

In neighbouring New Jersey, there were multiple reports of closed roads and bridges, and images of floodwater blanketing city streets.

"This is wild," an Ocean City, New Jersey-based blogger said in a video, external posted on social media, as he waded through water splashing above his waist.

Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to severe weather

The number of homes reporting power cuts peaked at close to a million on Thursday evening - with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey badly affected.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said utility providers were working tirelessly to restore power. In Maryland, almost two million customers were asked by authorities to limit their water consumption to essential use only due to "intermittent power disruptions".

The storm is expected to ease on Friday and move into the Canadian provinces of Nova Scotia and Newfoundland on Saturday, leaving a much drier weekend for the north-eastern United States, according to the Met Office.

However, another deep area of low pressure will likely arrive on Monday - bringing another spell of heavy rain and strong winds, and some further travel disruption.

The particularly high tide in California caused huge waves to crash over the wall in Pacifica, where a portion of the municipal pier collapsed

On the West Coast, the concern was for exceptionally high tides and the associated risk of flooding.

Both San Diego and Los Angeles reported a high tide of over 8ft (2.4m) earlier this week, and beach-goers were advised to avoid coastal areas.

Train services along the Amtrak Pacific Surfliner, which runs along the California coastline, cancelled several trains due to "washout conditions from high tides", the company shared on social media.

Dramatic footage from Oregon showed a man and a dog being swept into the sea by a fierce, so-called king tide - but both escaped unharmed, police said.

Watch: Man and dog narrowly escape powerful king tide in Oregon

In Miami, some travel delays persisted into Thursday after a FedEx plane overshot the runway the night before, which prompted the closure of all but one runway at the airport for a brief period.

A statement FedEx provided to US media confirmed that one of its flights had "experienced an issue upon landing". No injuries were reported, and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating what happened.

An airport employee who spoke anonymously to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, raised the possibility that rainy conditions had been a factor.

The American Automobile Association (AAA) predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for the Thanksgiving holiday over a seven-day period.

Another incredible...
articles.body_text:
Dawn Olivieri, who is starring in "Homestead: The Series," explains how giving up control of her Hollywood career led to more acting opportunities and a new life in rural Arkansas.

Another incredible nature video has hit the web.

As our loyal readers and OutKick Outdoors followers know, there aren't many things on the internet more entertaining than wildlife footage.

It gets the blood pumping and tends to be incredibly unpredictable. That's what makes it so much fun and enjoyable.

VIRAL WILDLIFE VIDEO CAPTURES DEER FLIPPING BOBCAT INTO THE AIR DURING WILD CONFRONTATION

A bull elk stands in Colorado during rutting season. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Facebook user Billy Fabian recently shared footage of an elk fending off a pair of wolves that wanted to mix it up.

It didn't go well for the wolves, one of them specifically.

A bull elk keeps his eyes on the cows gathered around him during rut season along S. St. Rain Avenue in Estes Park, Colo., on Thursday, Sept. 25, 2025. (Denver Post via Getty Images)

The large male elk stood its ground and then jacked up one of the wolves with its antlers. That's a lesson the wolf probably won't forget in the near future. The incident occurred in Wyoming, according to Whiskey Riff.

VIRAL VIDEO CAPTURES TWO MASSIVE BUCKS IN INTENSE ANTLER FIGHT DURING DEER RUT IN TEXAS

Check out the awesome footage below, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

That's definitely some of the best footage that we've seen in a long time. It's also a blunt reminder of the size difference between elks and wolves.

An adult male elk in North America can weigh up to 1,000 pounds. Many wolves don't break 100 pounds. That's a significant gap in weight.

I guess we have weight classes in boxing for a reason, and it's no different in the animal kingdom when it comes to raw power.

A wild bull elk rests and forages alone in a prairie at the forest edge during autumn foliage season. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

articles.title: US pilot tells Trump which fighter jet is ‘world’s greatest’ during Thanksgiving phone call
articles.excerpt: President Donald Trump, during a Thanksgiving call with Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Brant Smith, asked which fighter jet was the best. Smith told him it was the F-16. Trump made calls to service memb...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump, during a Thanksgiving call with Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Brant Smith, asked which fighter jet was the best. Smith told him it was the F-16. Trump made calls to service members of all six U.S. military branches.

President Donald Trump learned what the "world's greatest" fighter jet is, according to an F-16 pilot, during a phone call on Thanksgiving Day.

"So could I ask, before I give my little speech to you — a little quick one — could I ask, so the F-16, you love it, right?" Trump asked U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Brant Smith.

"World's greatest fighter jet, sir," Smith replied.

Trump spoke to Smith from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida as the president and first lady Melania made calls to service members from all six branches of the U.S. military.

A LOOK AT HOW THE TRUMPS SPEND THEIR THANKSGIVING HOLIDAY THROUGH THE YEARS

First lady Melania Trump makes Thanksgiving calls to U.S. service members next to President Donald Trump from Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, on November 26, 2026. (REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque)

Trump asked Smith to compare his F-16 to other fighter jets like the F-22 or F-35, to which Smith replied: "The F-16 all day."

TRUMP SAYS AIR FORCE PILOTS DESCRIBED A ROUND UFO FLYING THREE TIMES FASTER THAN AN F-22 FIGHTER JET

"You couldn't pay me to switch airplanes," Smith added.

"I love flying this airplane. And I think there are very few pilots in this room that would argue with me. Both of those airplanes (F-22 and F-35) are great, and they have their place in the world and in the war. But, this is a lot of fun. We get to do it all, and it does it all very well," Smith said.

A U.S. Air Force F-16 fighter jet is seen patrolling the skies above the Middle East as "American forces maintain regional presence and vigilance," according to U.S. Central Command. CENTCOM confirmed late Friday that American forces repelled multiple Iranian drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. (CENTCOM)

The president also asked Smith about his service and queried about what he was doing at the time.

"We are pre-installing the air base in Saudi Arabia," Smith replied.

CENTCOM'S THANKSGIVING MESSAGE TO TROOPS 'IS ONE OF DEEP GRATITUDE' FOR THEIR 'EXCEPTIONAL WORK' PROTECTING US

"You have a pretty large crowd of pilots, maintainers and ops support personnel from the 510th Expeditionary Fighter Squadron, the Buzzards. We're an F-16 unit. We've been on here since about ten days before Epic Fury kicked off. And we're flying combat operations out in the straits every day," he continued.

Trump complimented Smith on the military's efforts in the Middle East and in the war with Iran.

TRUMP PAUSES TURKEY PARDON TO SALUTE US TROOPS GUARDING STRAIT OF HORMUZ: 'WATCH OVER AND PROTECT'

"And you're seeing some big victories, aren't you? Knocking them out left and right, knocking out the launchers, knocking out the missiles, knocking out left and right. Amazing job you're doing, Brant," Trump said.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN UNLEASHED MISSILE, DRONE SURGE AFTER MIDTERMS

President Donald Trump participates in a call with U.S. service members from his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Thanksgiving Day on November 27, 2025, in Palm Beach, Florida. (Pete Marovich/Getty Images)

Smith also told the president he believes Iran was "starting to run out of things." Trump concurred.

"Yep. I think they are. I think they are. And that'll continue. And we're getting stronger. We sent an extra aircraft carrier," Trump said, referring to the Nimitz-class USS Theodore Roosevelt, which arrived in the Middle East on Nov. 16 to relieve USS George Washington.

US RACES TO BUILD BUNKERS ACROSS MIDDLE EAST AS IRANIAN STRIKES THREATEN AMERICAN TROOPS

"In my opinion, they're not very smart. They're making big mistakes. They've made a lot of mistakes. Their economy is down the tubes," the president said of Iran.

"Every day the stellar F-16 squadron is conducting missions across the Middle East to defend our interests and our assets. Like few people could ever even think about. This year, you've flown more than 2,000 sorties over more than 12,000 hours across eight different operations, including Operation Epic Fury. And you're getting plenty of time out there, aren't you, Brant?"

"Yes, sir," Smith said, adding, "Nine months and 10 days."

"Yeah, we're having fun," Smith said. "This is what we trained for."

"Amazing. The best in the world," Trump replied.

"You couldn't pay me to switch airplanes," Smith added.

"I love flying this airplane. And I think there are very few pilots in this room that would argue with me. Both of those airplanes (F-22 and F-35) are great, and they have their place in the world and in the war. But, this is a lot of fun. We get to do it all, and it does it all very well," Smith said.

A U.S. Air Force F-16 fighter jet is seen patrolling the skies above the Middle East as "American forces maintain regional presence and vigilance," according to U.S. Central Command. CENTCOM confirmed late Friday that American forces repelled multiple Iranian drone attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. (CENTCOM)

The president also asked Smith about his service and queried about what he was doing at the time.

"We are pre-installing the air base in Saudi Arabia," Smith replied.

CENTCOM'S THANKSGIVING MESSAGE TO TROOPS 'IS ONE OF DEEP GRATITUDE' FOR THEIR 'EXCEPTIONAL WORK' PROTECTING US

"You have a pretty large crowd of pilots, maintainers and ops support personnel from the 510th Expeditionary Fighter Squadron, the Buzzards. We're an F-16 unit. We've been on here since about ten days before Epic Fury kicked off. And we're flying combat operations out in the straits every day," he continued.

Trump complimented Smith on the military's efforts in the Middle East and in the war with Iran.

TRUMP PAUSES TURKEY PARDON TO SALUTE US TROOPS GUARDING STRAIT OF HORMUZ: 'WATCH OVER AND PROTECT'

"And you're seeing some big victories, aren't you? Knocking them out left and right, knocking out the launchers, knocking out the missiles, knocking out left and right. Amazing job you're doing, Brant," Trump said.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN UNLEASHED MISSILE, DRONE SURGE AFTER MIDTERMS

President Donald Trump participates in a call with U.S. service members from his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Thanksgiving Day on November 27, 2025, in Palm Beach, Florida. (Pete Marovich/Getty Images)

Smith also told the president he believes Iran was "starting to run out of things." Trump concurred.

"Yep. I think they are. I think they are. And that'll continue. And we're getting stronger. We sent an extra aircraft carrier," Trump said, referring to the Nimitz-class USS Theodore Roosevelt, which arrived in the Middle East on Nov. 16 to relieve USS George Washington.

US RACES TO BUILD BUNKERS ACROSS MIDDLE EAST AS IRANIAN STRIKES THREATEN AMERICAN TROOPS

"In my opinion, they're not very smart. They're making big mistakes. They've made a lot of mistakes. Their economy is down the tubes," the president said of Iran.

"Every day the stellar F-16 squadron is conducting missions across the Middle East to defend our interests and our assets. Like few people could ever even think about. This year, you've flown more than 2,000 sorties over more than 12,000 hours across eight different operations, including Operation Epic Fury. And you're getting plenty of time out there, aren't you, Brant?"

"Yes, sir," Smith said, adding, "Nine months and 10 days."

"Yeah, we're having fun," Smith said. "This is what we trained for."

"Amazing. The best in the world," Trump replied.

articles.title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
articles.excerpt: Hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tact...
articles.body_text:
Hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reuters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.

In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it “does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.”

Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force’s IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay or logistics and maintenance.

Among them are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air defense radar and other data feeds from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 U.S. Air Force locations around the world.

SAIC was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request seeking comment. Leidos referred questions to the Air Force.

Cloud One is among the U.S. military’s biggest cloud platforms, according to two of the sources.

“A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources said.

Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the U.S. military’s cyber force, to assess the damage, one of the sources said.

Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment.

The discovery of the hack led to a range of disruption. Two of the sources, along with a fourth person familiar with the matter, said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused.

Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said that some users had their administrator rights revoked.

All five sources spoke on condition of anonymity.

One source said that the cyber intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. That person likened the control plane to a universal remote, as intruders in theory could leverage their access to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts, though it was unclear whether the hackers did so in this case.

Reuters could not identify the specific vulnerability exploited by the hackers.

News of the breach comes amid heightened anxiety over AI-powered intrusions, a particularly serious problem for cloud-based networks because of the ability of AI models to swiftly detect weaknesses across wide surface areas.

The U.S. government already has been dealing with the fallout from at least six other recently disclosed cyber incidents, including two at the FBI, a previous hack of Pentagon data, a recent leak of Department of Homeland Security personnel information, a breach affecting at least two spy agencies and a hack at the Treasury Department.

Cloud One has long been in the crosshairs of hackers.

In a 2023 commentary carried by the online publication FedScoop, Cloud One’s leadership touted what they called a “100% success rate” in beating back what they said was a “staggering” number of attempts to penetrate the platform.

“There is no room for error when it comes to security,” Cloud One’s leadership wrote.

articles.title: Why is Israel celebrating Costa Rica’s ban on Francesca Albanese?
articles.excerpt:
Costa Rica has banned United Nations independent rapporteur Francesca Albanese from entering the country over what officials described as the risk she poses to national security.

Albanese has been on...
articles.body_text:
Costa Rica has banned United Nations independent rapporteur Francesca Albanese from entering the country over what officials described as the risk she poses to national security.

Albanese has been one of Israel’s foremost critics, documenting its genocidal war on Gaza as well as its systematic discrimination against Palestinians and illegal settlement in occupied Palestinian territory since 1967.

Albanese was stopped by police on security grounds on Thursday as she arrived at Juan Santamaria international airport in the capital San Jose, where she was due to be presented with an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica.

Albanese, who called the move “a disgrace”, was still being held at the airport on Friday.

Omer Badilla, the director-general of Costa Rica’s immigration authority, later appeared to offer some explanation on social media, saying Albanese “was refused entry to the country because she is the subject of an international alert due to links to terrorist acts”, without specifying the nature of that alert or which country had issued it.

“It is important to note that when national security is at risk, as is the case here,” Badilla continued without elaborating. “Our police authorities strictly enforce the provisions of our legal system.”

While the move was welcomed by Israel, including by its Ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, a number of Costa Rican and regional figures and rights groups, as well as the University of Costa Rica, have objected to the treatment of Albanese and demanded an explanation.

On Thursday, the Association of Human Rights Lawyers, Judges and Prosecutors of Latin America and the Caribbean (AJUFIDH) urged the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights to seek answers from the Costa Rican government, arguing that the ban may violate international obligations protecting UN experts.

Costa Rican lawmakers from several political parties have also criticised the move, describing it as arbitrary and damaging to the country’s reputation for defending human rights and international law, while the university has formally requested that immigration authorities and foreign ministry officials explain the legal grounds for the decision.

As Special Rapporteur, Albanese has used her position to document Israeli violations of international law. She accuses Israel of committing genocide in Gaza, maintaining an apartheid system against Palestinians and pursuing territorial expansion through illegal settlements in occupied East Jerusalem and the West Bank.

In her March 2024 report, Anatomy of a Genocide, for which she received numerous threats, Albanese found that there were reasonable grounds to conclude that Israel had committed acts prohibited under the UN Genocide Convention. She subsequently called for an arms embargo, sanctions against Israel and an end to the trade and financial relationships sustaining its occupation.

Throughout her tenure, Albanese has repeatedly described the occupation of Palestinian territory as an entrenched system of apartheid and settler colonialism, arguing that the displacement of Palestinians and expansion of illegal Israeli settlements are part of a much wider process of territorial dispossession.

She has also challenged Israel’s international backers, accusing governments of providing diplomatic protection and military assistance while failing to uphold their obligations under international law.

In her July 2025 report, she went further still, naming companies including Microsoft, Amazon and Google, alongside arms manufacturers and financial institutions, which she said were helping to sustain Israel’s occupation and military campaign. She called on governments to sever trade and financial ties with Israel, impose an arms embargo and hold companies accountable.

On Friday, Balkees Jarrah, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch, told Al Jazeera: “The Costa Rican authorities’ decision to bar Francesca Albanese entry comes in the context of increasing efforts aimed at muzzling criticism of Israeli authorities’ atrocity crimes against Palestinians, ensuring impunity for these abuses, and other governments’ complicity in them.”

Born to a lawyer and a homemaker in a small town in the Campania region of southern Italy in 1977, Albanese has said her interest in Israeli-Palestinian politics was shaped by her father’s library, where she encountered the writings of Holocaust survivor Primo Levi. She was also inspired by her older brother’s bedroom posters supporting Palestine during the first Intifada.

After studying law at the University of Pisa and human rights at SOAS in London, she pursued a career with the UN, first in Africa, then in Geneva and finally in Jerusalem with UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, before going on to be appointed Special Rapporteur on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories in May 2022.

Israel and its supporters have been campaigning against Albanese for years, repeatedly accusing her of anti-Semitism and anti-Israel bias and calling for her removal from her UN post.

The campaign intensified in 2023, when Israel and pro-Israel organisations stepped up demands for her dismissal following allegations that some of her public comments crossed the line into anti-Semitism.

In January that year, 11 US members of Congress signed a bipartisan letter urging the UN to remove her, while Israeli government officials also called for her resignation. Albanese rejected the accusations, saying they were intended to discredit her work documenting Israeli abuses.

The most significant escalation came in July 2025, when the Trump administration imposed sanctions against Albanese, accusing her of pursuing a campaign of political and economic warfare against Israel and the United States.

The measures included restrictions on Albanese entering the US, blocking her property and financial interests subject to US jurisdiction and prohibiting US nationals from engaging in transactions with her, effectively isolating her from much of the US financial system.

The US decision was roundly condemned by the UN and various rights groups.

A committee of the UN’s Human Rights Council characterised it as just one aspect of the “continued assault of the current US administration on the entire UN system and its core values of human rights, justice, accountability and the rule of law”. Rights groups, including Human Rights Watch (HRW) and Amnesty International, also criticised the decision, with the latter slamming the US measures as a “disgraceful affront to international justice”.

San Francisco 49ers star Kyle Juszczyk gives his blessing for a possible George Kittle WWE run.

It’s no secret that George Kittle is a huge WWE fan, specifically of Penta – who is the current men’s Money in the Bank contract holder.

Kittle showed love for Penta last weekend when the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Mexico City to take on the Minnesota Vikings. Kittle, who entered the building with Penta’s mask on his head, hit the Lucha Libre star’s "Cero Miedo" celebration when he scored his first touchdown. He finished with two on the night.

San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy and tight end George Kittle answer questions after an NFL game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. (AP Photo/Fernando Llano)

The star tight end has been candid about his interest in joining WWE when his football career is finished. His teammate, two-time All-Pro fullback Kyle Juszczyk, gave him his own personal blessing in a recent interview as part of OutKick Dropkick.

"As a kid, I loved WWE. Me and my brothers, we would have our own WWE matches in the living room. We’d set up the cushions from the couches on the floor," he said. "We’d powerbomb each other into the sofa and stuff. I loved it as a kid. So, I definitely have an appreciation for that.

Following the 49ers’ victory, Kittle donned a unique mask that featured the San Francisco 49ers’ gold and red. It also had Kittle’s No. 85 on it. He also had a Penta shirt on.

"I love Penta. He's awesome," he said. "I met Penta like eight or nine years ago. I watched him wrestle like five different times for five different companies. It was awesome. And then the following year, I got to meet him, did a jersey swap with him, and we just kind of been in contact ever since.

"I completely took his ‘Cero Miedo’ because I think it's just, I like the confidence that it exudes. And I just think he's an awesome wrestler. I'm so happy that he's in the WWE now. It's really fun."

Kittle did get involved in a match once. He gave The Miz a clothesline at WrestleMania 39, allowing Pat McAfee to pick up a victory.

articles.title: Wife of Patrick Mahomes unleashes fire and fury towards refs after botched call in Buffalo
articles.excerpt:
NFL Referees did the unthinkable last night, they called a game-changing penalty on the Kansas City Chiefs, and Craig Carton is loving every second of it.

Thursday delivered us quite possibly the gre...
articles.body_text:
NFL Referees did the unthinkable last night, they called a game-changing penalty on the Kansas City Chiefs, and Craig Carton is loving every second of it.

Thursday delivered us quite possibly the greatest slate of Thanksgiving football games of all time, and it ended with a bang.

Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills stunned the Kansas City Chiefs at the buzzer, 13-10, thanks in large part to a blocked punt in the waning seconds. The Bills deflected the kick, it was returned by Greg Dortch to Kansas City's 39, and Tyler Bass drilled the long field goal to walk it off.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

It was the perfect day of football — including two stunning comebacks in Detroit and Dallas. Again, I'd argue it was the greatest Thanksgiving slate ever.

BUFFALO BILLS OUTLAST KANSAS CITY CHIEFS IN DEFENSIVE STRUGGLE TO MAINTAIN TOP SEED STATUS IN AFC

Tommy Doman Jr. No. 39 and Tyler Bass No. 16 of the Buffalo Bills warm up before the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, N.Y., on Nov. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

Of course — because we can't have nice things — it didn't come without some controversy at the end. In another stunning turn of events, this one actually worked against the Chiefs!

That's right. Rashee Rice had a catch overturned late in the fourth quarter that took away a Kansas City first down, even though it certainly looked like a catch. The refs looked it over, decided it didn't count, and forced the Chiefs to punt instead.

You rarely see a call go against the Chiefs. It's been a running joke amongst NFL fans for years now. So, yes, seeing one screw them over was a stunner.

Don't take my word for it, though! Just ask Brittany Mahomes, the firecracker wife of star QB Patrick Mahomes:

"Guess we can't even play football without it getting called against us," Mahomes said, via her Instagram story after the game. "Not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s–t anymore from anyone."

Incredible. Again, seeing a call go against the Chiefs was shocking. You just don't see it. You haven't seen it during the Mahomes era. Not saying I agree with the call, by the way, because I'm not sure I do.

I think it was probably a catch. It was ruled that way on the field, so I'm not sure how they would overturn it based on that video evidence. I just don't see that ball move. Even Mike Tirico had to squint to see it.

THE ABSOLUTE WORST CALL OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON HAPPENED LAST NIGHT WHILE YOU WERE SLEEPING

Patrick Mahomes of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts in the second quarter against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, N.Y., on Nov. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

Brittany Mahomes attends the 2024 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Launch Party at Hard Rock Hotel on May 16, 2024, in New York City. (WireImage)

If that's not a catch, I'm not sure what we're doing anymore. And I'm not a Chiefs fan, believe me. I don't love defending them here, but fair is fair, and that was probably a bogus reversal.

Par the course for the refs, though. They've been HORRIBLE this week. They screwed over the Jags in New York on Sunday, then awarded Mike Evans a fake touchdown Sunday night, and then completely botched a call in Tuesday's MACtion game between Kent State and Eastern Michigan.

And now, they have me defending the Kansas City Chiefs and Brittany Mahomes!

articles.title: Treasure hunters searching a field uncover 5,500-coin hoard hiding 'national treasure'
articles.excerpt: Archaeologists in Sweden unearthed 45 ancient Roman silver coins and a gold ring during excavations ahead of a military base expansion. The treasure, believed to have been buried around 1,500 years ag...
articles.body_text:
Archaeologists in Sweden unearthed 45 ancient Roman silver coins and a gold ring during excavations ahead of a military base expansion. The treasure, believed to have been buried around 1,500 years ago, included two coins suspected of being counterfeits.

Archaeologists in Norway have uncovered an extraordinarily rare 1,000-year-old coin minted during the reign of Viking King Olaf Haraldsson, better known as Saint Olaf, inside the largest Viking Age coin hoard ever found in the country.

The discovery, announced by the Museum of Cultural History in Oslo, marks the first time a coin of this type has been found in Norway since 1924.

The Olaf coin went on display Nov. 20 at the Historical Museum in Oslo — part of the University of Oslo's Museum of Cultural History — as part of a new exhibition showcasing the Mørstad Hoard.

PUZZLING SOUND IN BACKYARD LEADS HOMEOWNER TO MASSIVE 1,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE

The hoard was originally discovered on April 10 by metal detectorists Vegard Sørlie and Rune Sætre in Rena, Innlandet County, and the site has since been secured and investigated for further research.

Officials said the latest count puts the cache at 5,500 coins, though researchers believe the total could soon exceed 6,000.

Archaeologists in Norway uncovered an extraordinarily rare 1,000-year-old coin minted during the reign of Viking King Olaf Haraldsson, shown at left. (Bettmann via Getty Images; Tea Kristiansen/Museum of Cultural History)

The star of the hoard, officials said, is a coin depicting Haraldsson, who ruled from 1015 to 1028.

Haraldsson, who became a saint after his death, occupies "a unique place in Norwegian history," officials said.

RARE COIN BEARING FACE OF KING WITH INFAMOUS NICKNAME UNEARTHED AFTER 1,000 YEARS

"Fewer than 20 of his coins have survived to the present day, and most have been found outside Norway," the release said.

"Only four examples of the type found in the Mørstad Hoard have previously been discovered, including just one in Norway."

Dating between 1024 and 1028, the Olaf Haraldsson coin may have been in circulation for up to 25 years before it was deposited in the Mørstad Hoard, officials said. (Lill-Ann Chepstow-Lusty/Museum of Cultural History)

The new coin was spotted by archaeologist Anne Skogsfjord, who immediately ran to tell a colleague about the find.

Officials said the coin was initially thought to be Anglo-Saxon and had been roughly sorted into the group of coins issued by Æthelred II.

MYSTERIOUS FIND BENEATH FIELD LEADS MAN TO MASSIVE TREASURE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES

"I could see that it read ONLAF R+ NORMANORV … Could this really be a coin of Olaf Haraldsson that I was holding?" Skogsfjord said. "And it was! It was a very special moment."

She added, "I realized that we had found a national treasure."

"When you think this Viking treasure cannot become any more exciting, new surprises emerge."

The coin dates between 1024 and 1028, and officials said it may have been in circulation for up to 25 years before it was deposited in the hoard.

Featuring a cross on both sides, the coin shows how Olaf used currency to legitimize the Christian faith and establish himself as a Christian king of European standing, according to numismatics expert Svein H. Gullbekk.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The museum added, "Few archaeological and historical sources can be directly linked to Olaf Haraldsson himself. Numismatic sources — the coins — were closely connected to the king."

Gullbekk said in the release, "Olaf Haraldsson himself decided what these coins should look like, and perhaps he was present when they were struck. It is entirely possible that this very coin from Mørstad was once held in the king's own hand."

Hanna Geiran, Norway's director general of cultural heritage, said the coin "is not only a rare object, but also tangible testimony from a time when the foundations of the Norwegian kingdom and the Christianization of the country were laid."

Archaeologist Anne Skogsfjord, seen at left, spotted the rare Olaf Haraldsson coin during cataloging and immediately ran to tell a colleague about the find. (Tea Kristiansen/Museum of Cultural History; Lill-Ann Chepstow-Lusty/Museum of Cultural History)

"When you think this Viking treasure cannot become any more exciting, new surprises emerge," said Geiran, the museum noted.

"This St. Olaf coin is yet another reminder of how extraordinary this find is."

Looking ahead, the museum said that research on the coin hoard will continue "for a long time to come."

"Every single coin must undergo the same thorough process before entering the museum collection," added officials. "Numismatists, archaeologists, conservators, collection managers and photographers are all involved."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The Mørstad Hoard joins several other significant European coin discoveries unearthed in recent months.

The Museum of Cultural History said research on the 5,500-coin Mørstad Hoard will continue "for a long time to come," with numismatists, archaeologists, conservators, collection managers and photographers examining every coin. (Tea Kristiansen/Museum of Cultural History; Lill-Ann Chepstow-Lusty/Museum of Cultural History)

Earlier this year, archaeologists in Germany uncovered 11 ancient Celtic coins at a construction site — the largest hoard of its kind ever found in the region, dating back more than 2,000 years.

Meanwhile, in Finland, a metal detectorist recently unearthed a Viking Age silver cache holding around 4,000 coins, jewelry and other artifacts.

Andrea Margolis is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital and Fox Business. Readers can follow her on X at @andreamargs or send story tips to andrea.margolis@fox.com.

articles.title: Josh Holloway reveals Kevin Costner's high standards on the Yellowstone set before his exit
articles.excerpt:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld disses the Emmy Awards for leaving Chuck Norris out of the 'In Memoriam' program, discusses Taylor Sheridan's productions and more on 'Gutfeld!'

Josh Holloway is pulling ba...
articles.body_text:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld disses the Emmy Awards for leaving Chuck Norris out of the 'In Memoriam' program, discusses Taylor Sheridan's productions and more on 'Gutfeld!'

Josh Holloway is pulling back the curtain on what life was like on the set of "Yellowstone."

The neo-Western series created by Taylor Sheridan dominated TV for all five of its seasons. The success of Sheridan's crowning achievement also led to multiple prequels and spinoffs.

The "Yellowstone" universe is a powerhouse, and Holloway played a major role. He starred as villain Roarke Morris in season three of the series, and very briefly appeared in season four.

LUKE GRIMES SAYS HE HASN'T SPOKEN TO KEVIN COSTNER SINCE 'YELLOWSTONE'

Kevin Costner as John Dutton in the hit TV show "Yellowstone." ((Credit: Paramount Network via Paramount Press Site))

Now, he's shining a light on what Kevin Costner was like on set, and the high standards and work ethic the legendary actor brought to the series.

Holloway recently appeared on the "Inside of You" podcast hosted by Michael Rosenbaum, and explained that Costner wasn't afraid to call himself out on set when he didn't perform at a high level.

ZOE SALDAÑA SAYS TAYLOR SHERIDAN GIVES STARS TWO CHOICES: 'MAKE SURE THAT YOU DON'T F--K UP... OR YOU QUIT'

The "Yellowstone" universe continues to expand. ((Credit: Paramount Network/Paramount+ Media Site))

"What I was impressed with with him, he did a close-up with me where he’s telling me about the rules or something, and he did it, and he just went inside and he was like, ‘Ah, that sh*t was lazy.’ And then he came up and I was like, ‘He cares. He’s still working.’ And he brought it. He's in this. So, I was impressed with that. You know, that he’s still keeping his standard high. I respected that. I was like, ‘Hell yeah,'" Holloway explained.

You can watch Holloway's comments in the video below starting around 1:05:00, and let me know your thoughts at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

'YELLOWSTONE' STAR NEAL MCDONOUGH REFUSES TO WATCH HIT SERIES FOR ‘PAINFUL’ REASON

It's worth noting that while Costner might have held himself to extremely high standards on set, his time on "Yellowstone" didn't end in great fashion.

Costner infamously split from the show during the mid-season split in season five, and never returned to ever play John Dutton again.

His exit, which led to plenty of reports of feuds behind the scenes, resulted in the final "Yellowstone" episodes feeling a bit rushed and an ending that never truly felt complete.

Don't get me wrong. The conclusion of "Yellowstone" was always clear to anyone paying attention, but without John Dutton, something just felt a little unsatisfied.

UNIVERSAL CITY, CALIFORNIA - MAY 08: Josh Holloway arrives at the Los Angeles premiere of Max Original Series "Duster" at Universal Studios Hollywood on May 08, 2025 in Universal City, California. ((Photo by Maya Dehlin Spach/WireImage via Getty Images))

What do you think about Costner and the "Yellowstone" universe? Let me know at David.Hookstead@outkick.com.

David Hookstead is a reporter for OutKick.

articles.title: Nebraska Cornhuskers look to pull another upset as Iowa Hawkeyes eye college football playoff path
articles.excerpt:
Check out the best moments from the Week 12 matchup between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Nebraska Cornhuskers with commentary from Gus Johnson and Joel Klatt.

It was another wild week of College F...
articles.body_text:
Check out the best moments from the Week 12 matchup between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Nebraska Cornhuskers with commentary from Gus Johnson and Joel Klatt.

It was another wild week of College Football, and frankly, my picks were garbage. It has been a rough stretch in the football season for me overall. Mostly a roller coaster ride. I’ve had some really bad stretches and a really good stretch. Now that we are hitting the home stretch of the season, we need to lock in and try to escape this year with a bit of profit. An uphill battle for me starts with this one between Nebraska and Iowa.

The Nebraska Cornhuskers aren’t having a terrible season, but they also aren’t going to make the College Football Playoffs. They wouldn’t even make it if the field was expanded this year. The team is 7-4, which is good enough to get them some Bowl Game consideration and likely a decent one. However, the team is just 4-4 in conference and won’t play in the conference championship, either. The Cornhuskers are certainly coming off their best win of the season as they took down the once-mighty Ohio State.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Isaiah Mozee #22 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers celebrates a first down against the Ohio State Buckeyes during the first half at Memorial Stadium on Nov. 21, 2026, in Lincoln, Neb. (Getty Images)

This was by far the best win of the season, but to their credit, they also hung in there against an Indiana team that has been good but shaky for most of this year. Nebraska opened the season with five straight wins, mostly over bad teams. They took down Ohio, Bowling Green, North Dakota, Michigan State, and Maryland. It wasn’t enough to make people think they were a great team, but certainly decent. Then they lost the next four games, dropping ones to Indiana and Oregon by three in each. They lost by a touchdown or more against Washington and Illinois.
