articles.title: Google Gemini may expose private emails to reviewers
articles.excerpt: Cybersecurity threats escalate as Leah Siskind analyzes Google’s warning about hackers using AI to automate cyberattacks against companies. Discussing the battle between defenders and attackers with J...
articles.body_text:
Cybersecurity threats escalate as Leah Siskind analyzes Google’s warning about hackers using AI to automate cyberattacks against companies. Discussing the battle between defenders and attackers with John Roberts, the FDD AI Research fellow references Anthropic’s release of advanced models months ago. Siskin warns that super advanced AI models now have the dangerous ‘ability to detect vulnerabilities’ in software systems.

Think about everything sitting in your Gmail inbox right now. Maybe there's a conversation with your doctor, a recent bank statement or a personal message you never intended anyone else to read. Your Google Drive may hold years of private documents. You probably don't spend much time thinking about who might see that information beyond the people you share it with. But what happens when you connect those services to Google's Gemini AI assistant?

An independent researcher has raised concerns about how Gemini handles information retrieved from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The findings prompted questions about whether some private content could end up in conversations reviewed by humans.

We contacted Google, and the company confirmed that some information retrieved from connected Gmail and Drive accounts may be seen by human reviewers under certain circumstances. Google stressed that these connections are off by default. Here's what you should know before giving Gemini access to your personal information.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU

Google's Gemini assistant can retrieve information from connected Gmail accounts to answer questions, raising concerns about how private emails may be handled. (Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images)

An independent researcher using the name thisisme6598 published findings on GitHub, raising questions about the way Gemini retrieves information from connected Gmail and Google Drive accounts. The researcher tested Gemini using a personal Google Account with connected apps enabled. According to the published findings, Gemini sometimes retrieved information from emails or files during conversations without someone explicitly asking it to search Gmail or Drive. For example, the researcher described asking Gemini whether an internet service bill seemed too expensive. During some tests, Gemini reportedly retrieved billing information from Gmail, including payment amounts, account details and confirmation numbers.

In certain instances, the researcher reported that Gemini returned several sentences directly from an email and, in some tests, the entire email, including its headers. The researcher argues that this behavior creates a privacy concern because information retrieved into a Gemini conversation may become eligible for human review. However, the published findings do not establish that a human reviewer actually accessed the researcher's emails. Google told CyberGuy that the reported retrieval was standard behavior for someone who had voluntarily connected their apps. The company also emphasized that retrieved files remain visible only to the authenticated account holder and are not exposed publicly through this process.

Yes, under certain circumstances. Google's own Connected Apps privacy documentation confirms that trained human reviewers, including service providers, may review a subset of information processed through Gemini's connected apps. That information can include summaries or excerpts from relevant Gmail messages and Google Drive documents.

In some cases, Google acknowledges that reviewers may see a complete email or file if it is short or especially relevant to the request. Google also says human reviewers may access some Gmail inbox content when investigating abuse or harm or responding to submitted feedback.

The company uses these reviews to evaluate Gemini's responses and improve its services.

Simply using Gmail or Google Drive does not subject your private content to this review process. The concern involves information retrieved after someone voluntarily connects those services to consumer Gemini. Google says it does not train generative AI models directly on someone's entire Gmail inbox or Drive. However, relevant information processed during Gemini conversations may be used for model improvement, depending on account settings. Google specifically warns against connecting apps containing confidential information someone would be uncomfortable having a reviewer see.

We contacted Google directly to ask whether human reviewers could access Gmail messages or Drive files processed through the consumer Gemini app. We also asked whether the company had changed its privacy disclosures, notified existing customers and provided ways to prevent human review. A Google spokesperson told CyberGuy:

"Gmail and Google Drive’s core privacy protections remain unchanged, and your private emails and files are not reviewed by humans simply by using Gmail, Drive, or built-in Workspace features. Connecting those apps to the consumer Gemini app is off by default — it’s an optional way to get more personalized, time-saving answers across your Google apps when you want them. Users can disconnect their apps in Gemini settings at any time without losing access to Gemini’s core features."

Google also confirmed that when someone connects their apps to consumer Gemini with activity saving enabled, a small subset of conversations may undergo human review. Those conversations can contain relevant information retrieved from connected services. Before trained service providers review the material, Google says it separates the conversations from the associated Google Account and takes steps to reduce identifying information. The company also disputes the suggestion that the researcher's findings demonstrate public exposure of private files.

Another part of the controversy involves changes to Google's public privacy disclosures. In Oct. 2023, Google published a blog post about its approach to generative AI privacy. The company said that content from Gmail, Docs and Drive accessed through Bard's Workspace extensions would not be seen by human reviewers or used to train the Bard model.

On Oct. 16, 2026, Google added an update to that same blog post. The new language explains that Google has introduced additional optional features allowing people to connect Workspace information to other Google services. Google says that when someone enables these newer features, a subset of the information may be used to train generative AI models, depending on their settings. It may also undergo human review in limited circumstances. The researcher argues that the change represents a reversal of Google's earlier privacy commitment.

However, Google's original statement concerned Bard's Workspace extensions, while the updated disclosure addresses newer connected features. The available evidence does not establish that Google quietly changed the underlying handling of information in existing connections. We asked Google whether people who previously connected their accounts were notified about the updated disclosures or asked to provide additional consent. Google's response did not directly address those questions. Instead, the company emphasized that the newer connections are optional and can be disabled. That leaves an important question about how clearly Google communicates changes to its AI privacy practices, particularly as new features gain access to more personal information.

APPLE TIGHTENS MAC SECURITY AS AI AGENTS SEEK YOUR FILES

Google Workspace with Gemini brings AI features to Google's productivity tools, with different data privacy protections for business accounts than for personal Gemini accounts. (Photo by Felix Zahn/Photothek via Getty Images)

Google says it disconnects conversations from the associated Google Account before sending them to trained service providers for routine review. The company also takes steps to reduce personal information. However, removing account identifiers does not necessarily eliminate every sensitive detail contained in an email excerpt or document summary.

Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub explains that conversations reviewed by service providers may be retained for up to three years, even after someone deletes the corresponding activity from their Google Account.

Turning off Gemini's History setting, previously called Keep Activity, prevents future conversations from being used to train generative AI models unless someone submits feedback. However, Google may still process conversations for security and safety purposes, including with help from human reviewers.

On Nov. 16, 2026, Google announced changes to its Gemini privacy controls. Under the previous policy, Google retained conversations for up to 72 hours when Keep Activity was turned off. Under the new policy, Google will retain conversations for approximately two months when History is turned off. The company is rolling out these changes globally over several weeks.

If you use Gemini, it's worth checking which accounts and services you've connected. You may find that you don't need every feature enabled. Here are some settings worth reviewing.

Google groups Gmail and Drive under Google Workspace in its connected-app settings. Here's how to check the connection on a computer.

If you see a different menu, look for Connected Apps in Gemini's settings. Google offers different connection controls depending on account eligibility and available features. You can reconnect supported services later if you decide to use them.

If you want to prevent future conversations from being used to train Google's generative AI models, review this setting.

Turning off History stops future chats from being used to train generative AI models unless you choose to submit feedback. Some connected apps, including Google Workspace, become unavailable. Google may still process conversations for security and safety purposes. Depending on whether the latest privacy update has reached your account, conversations may be retained for up to 72 hours under the previous policy or approximately two months under the new policy.

WHAT YOUR INTERNET PROVIDER, WEBSITES AND ADVERTISERS SEE

Google's Personal Intelligence feature can connect Gemini to Gmail and other Google services, allowing the assistant to provide personalized responses using information from those accounts. (Photo Illustration by Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Google is introducing a separate privacy control that lets you keep your Gemini conversation history while opting out of generative AI model training. If the new setting is available on your account, here's how to find it on a computer.

Google says future chats will no longer be used to train generative AI models unless you submit feedback. However, human review may still occur for other service improvements and safety purposes. If you want to prevent Gemini from retrieving information from Gmail and Drive, disconnect Google Workspace separately.

Disconnecting an app does not automatically delete information from earlier Gemini conversations. Google says Gemini may still use information from previously saved chats even after you disconnect the original app. That's why it's important to both disconnect the app and delete conversations containing sensitive information.

Remember that previously reviewed information may remain subject to Google's separate retention policies, even after you delete your activity.

Think carefully before giving an AI assistant access to confidential documents or personal communications. If you don't need Gemini to retrieve information from Gmail or Drive, leave those connections disabled. Also, remember that uploading a document directly into Gemini creates a separate privacy consideration.

Google says uploaded content may be used to improve its services when History, previously called Keep Activity, is enabled, potentially with help from human reviewers. Whether that content is used to train generative AI models also depends on your training settings and whether you submit feedback.

Google says the connected-app disclosures involved in this controversy apply to personal Google Accounts using consumer Gemini. Business, Enterprise and Education accounts covered by Google Workspace commercial terms have different privacy protections. According to Google's response to CyberGuy, customer data governed by those commercial terms is not reviewed by humans or used to train foundational AI models.

If you use Gemini through an employer or school, your organization's settings and agreements determine which features are available and how information is handled. The important point is that the consumer Gemini privacy rules discussed here should not automatically be applied to commercial Workspace accounts.

I can understand why someone would want Gemini to search their Gmail or find a document buried in Google Drive. We've all wasted time digging through old emails looking for something we need. Having an AI assistant do that work sounds pretty appealing. But I think Google has a responsibility to make the privacy implications much clearer before someone connects an account. Most people probably don't expect information pulled from their private emails to become part of a conversation that could eventually be reviewed by another human being. I appreciate that Google responded to our questions and explained the safeguards it uses. Still, I would have liked a more direct answer about whether existing customers were notified when the privacy disclosures changed. If you're giving an AI assistant access to years of personal information, you deserve to know exactly how that information might be handled. Personally, I'd leave Gmail and Drive disconnected unless I had a specific reason to use those features.

Would you trust an AI assistant with access to years of your private emails if you knew some of that information could be seen by human reviewers? Or has Google crossed a privacy line, even with your permission? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

articles.title: Rare turtles found inside baggage at Amsterdam airport
articles.excerpt:
An official holds one of the seized Vallarta mud turtles - they are now receiving  care at a specialised sanctuary

Twenty-six "very rare" turtles have been seized from a traveller's checked baggage a...
articles.body_text:
An official holds one of the seized Vallarta mud turtles - they are now receiving  care at a specialised sanctuary

Twenty-six "very rare" turtles have been seized from a traveller's checked baggage at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport, a Dutch government agency has said.

The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said a man flying from Mexico to Hong Kong via the airport was arrested on Saturday after the Vallarta mud turtles were found by customs officers.

The endangered species, thought to be the smallest freshwater turtles in the world with a maximum length of about 10cm (4in), were wrapped in duct tape to prevent them from moving.

The NVWA said they were "presumably stolen" from the wild in their native Mexico.

It said most of the turtles were found in a box with a toy car, while the others were in a closed sock inside a suitcase.

The arrested man remains in custody and an investigation is under way.

Meanwhile, the turtles are receiving care at a "specialised sanctuary", the NVWA said.

In 2025, the US NGO Turtle Island estimated that no more than 300 Vallarta mud turtles existed in the wild.

They are listed as critically endangered on a list published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

According to environmental news outlet Mongabay, a Vallarta mud turtle can sell for $10,000 (£7,500) or more on the black market in Asia.

Other cases of live turtles being smuggled to Hong Kong have been reported this year.

In October, customs authorities in Hong Kong were reported to have seized eight turtles, external that were thought to be endangered. The reptiles had an estimated market value of about $54,000.

Three months prior, Hong Kong customs detected two separate smuggling cases, external. Some 42 live turtles, with a total estimated market value of $210,000 were seized.

articles.title: Why did Georgian police clash with Turkish football fans over Palestine?
articles.excerpt:
Police in Georgia have detained at least 16 people following clashes between football fans at a game between Turkish and Israeli clubs.

The Europa League fifth round match between Turkiye’s Besiktas ...
articles.body_text:
Police in Georgia have detained at least 16 people following clashes between football fans at a game between Turkish and Israeli clubs.

The Europa League fifth round match between Turkiye’s Besiktas and Israel’s Hapoel Be’er Sheva was hosted in Georgia instead of Turkiye.

The coastal Georgian city of Batumi was selected last month as a neutral territory to host the game for “safety and security reasons” because of fears of protests over Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, according to the European football association, UEFA.

Despite the precaution, tensions between fans spilled over into the stadium and the match was suspended for 30 minutes. Once play resumed, Besiktas won the game 2-1.

It is not the first time violent clashes have marred football matches involving Israeli clubs since Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza began in October 2023.

Here’s what we know about the latest unrest:

Tensions between fans had already been rising before kickoff in Batumi on Thursday.

According to the Georgian news outlet Civil Georgia, videos on social media showed groups of Besiktas fans marching through Batumi and physical confrontations between fans and police officers.

Turkiye’s Anadolu Agency reported that the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel opposition.

In the 26th minute, the game was temporarily suspended when clashes broke out between Georgian police and Besiktas supporters. Turkish media outlets reported that police entered the stands and used pepper spray against Turkish fans.

According to reports, the police involvement came after a fan displayed a Palestinian flag and banner.

Turkiye’s TRT World reported that police surrounded the fan and used pepper spray, adding that video later showed a Besiktas fan being carried out on a stretcher and others being injured during the intervention.

Omer Celik, spokesperson and deputy chairman of Turkiye’s ruling AK party, posted on X that the “intervention and violence” against the Besiktas fans who unfurled a ‘FREEDOM FOR PALESTINE’ banner and held a Palestine flag was “unacceptable”.

“Besiktas fans spoke on behalf of the alliance of humanity and became the voice of humanity. We strongly condemn the Israeli team’s provocations on the pitch. We extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to our fans who were injured in the incidents and taken to hospital. We are closely monitoring the condition of our citizens,” Celik said.

But Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili told reporters that UEFA officials confiscated the fans’ Palestine flags and Georgian state authorities played no role in the confiscation.

Tamazashvili said that 16 people were detained and three ministry employees injured.

“While marching from European Square towards Batumi Arena, some of the fans of the football club ‘Besiktas’ stood out by their aggressive actions,” the ministry said in a statement.

“They violated the public order by making indecent shouting and shooting of various objects, disobeyed the legal demands of the police, resisted law enforcement and physically confronted them.”

Police took appropriate measures to curb the violence, de-escalate incidents and ensure public safety, including the use of what it called “special means”, the ministry added.

It denied that the use of force was related to the display of pro-Palestine banners and flags.

“We categorically deny this information and emphasise that violent actions by fans and physical confrontation with law enforcers prior to the display of flags and banners have just begun while marching towards the stadium.”

Besiktas said it condemned the use of “disproportionate force”.

“We have initiated formal inquiries with our Consulate General in Batumi and with UEFA regarding the disproportionate force used by security personnel against our supporters; we will continue to monitor the situation closely until every single one of our supporters has returned home safely,” read a club statement.

In a post on X congratulating the Besiktas victory, the Turkish Football Federation said it would “closely monitor the unacceptable behaviour directed at our club, Besiktas and our supporters in Batumi tonight, and that we will take action with the relevant authorities to ensure that these incidents are fully investigated and the necessary steps are taken.”

Other Turkish Super Lig clubs, including Trabzonspor, Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, Erzurumspor, Basaksehir and Samsunspor, also condemned the use of force against Besiktas fans.

Since the onset of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza three years ago, Turkish clubs have not hosted Israeli opposition at home because of security concerns, with matches played in neutral territories instead.

Turkish-Israeli relations have taken a downturn since the war began, with Turkish authorities taking a hard line against the military policies of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government in the occupied Palestinian territories.

However, Georgia and Israel have good relations with close ties maintained amid the war.

Israel’s far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir was in the capital Tbilisi for a diplomatic visit last year.

Last year, English club Aston Villa hosted a Europa League game against Maccabi Tel Aviv, but security concerns prompted West Midlands Police to recommend the banning of Israeli fans from the game.

The decision was taken following violence after a match in Amsterdam between Maccabi and Dutch side Ajax. Police intervened against protesters and Israeli media framed the clashes as a “violent, anti-Semitic pogrom”.

In 2024, another match between Ajax and Maccabi Tel Aviv led to clashes between fans of the Israeli team and pro-Palestine protesters, as Maccabi fans burned Palestinian flags and attacked homes displaying them.

articles.title: Eisenkot navigates tricky waters as he tests power-sharing with Netanyahu
articles.excerpt:
The 2026 Israeli elections were termed the most consequential in recent decades for the country – for multiple reasons.

For Benjamin Netanyahu, the caretaker prime minister, and his right-wing coalit...
articles.body_text:
The 2026 Israeli elections were termed the most consequential in recent decades for the country – for multiple reasons.

For Benjamin Netanyahu, the caretaker prime minister, and his right-wing coalition, the elections were about keeping the far-right in power to protect the formative changes they enacted in state policies and institutions. For the anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot – or the “change bloc”, as it is referred to – the promise was to replace the failed October 7 government as they termed it, rehabilitate Israel’s international standing, and end internal divisions.

Once the results were announced, things changed. Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with forming Israel’s next government. But his bloc does not have enough seats in the Knesset to win a vote of confidence on its own. The United Arab List and the Joint List, parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, have 19 seats and are willing to back Eisenkot in his efforts to replace Netanyahu as Israel’s premier. But some in the change bloc, such as Avigdor Lieberman, promised not to support any government coalition that includes an Arab-led party or one that depended on votes from Palestinian citizens of Israel.

This, despite the fact that Lieberman himself became chair of the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee thanks to those same votes. That contradiction was pointed out by Mohamed Majadli, the chief editor of AlNas Radio in Israel and an analyst on the country’s Channel 12.

In such a limited space for political manoeuvres, Eisenkot embarked on forming a coalition, holding talks with his partners, while also trying to open channels of communication with ultra-Orthodox parties, particularly the United Torah Judaism party. At the same time, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett led efforts to form a unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud party and succeeded in convincing Eisenkot’s Yashar party to open formal talks with Likud.

The prospect of reneging on the change bloc’s central promise to oust Netanyahu looms large over these talks. Bennett and others are advocating for that outcome in light of the lack of a clear Zionist majority against Israel’s longest-serving prime minister.

Meanwhile, leader of the Democrats group, Yair Golan, has publicly opposed any unity formula with Netanyahu and has called out Bennett for his efforts to reach it. The Yashar-Likud talks are complex and overshadowed by, among other issues, accusations between the two sides.

Netanyahu accuses the change bloc of working to undermine Israel by working with Arab-led parties, which he has referred to as “the enemy”. Eisenkot has gone on the record saying that Netanyahu endangers the security of Israel and is willing to ignite war for his personal gain.

From Likud’s perspective, a unity government would require a rotation agreement on the premiership. That means that rather than getting rid of Netanyahu, Eisenkot would have to agree to Netanyahu staying on as prime minister for two years, or agreeing to serve second in the rotation.

This scenario gained traction after judges presiding over Netanyahu corruption trials recommended dropping the most serious charge of bribery, as well as reconsidering the charges or reaching a plea bargain in the others. This development has strengthened Netanyahu’s negotiating position and prompted him to call for an end to the political boycott against him.

Against this backdrop, Eisenkot is manoeuvring through dangerous political waters. If he fails to form a government, voters may be forced to return to the polls again while Netanyahu remains at the helm. This scenario could translate into a loss of support for the change bloc and hand Netanyahu a renewed mandate, while simultaneously ending the political careers of some leaders such as Eisenkot.

If Eisenkot chooses unity with Netanyahu over the promises he made to his voters, he will lose credibility among supporters. Additionally, Eisenkot could be outmanoeuvred by Netanyahu.

Many point to the coalition agreement between Benjamin Netanyahu and Benny Gantz in 2020, which included a rotating premiership. The government collapsed before Benny Gantz assumed his position and his political career never recovered.

In political terms, forming a unity government with Netanyahu would represent a reversal of election promises on fundamental issues such as transparency, judicial reform, and the influence of religion on the state, because unlike the change bloc, Netanyahu’s allies are already embedded in the state bureaucracy and able to entrench these policies.

More strategically, it reflects the knee-jerk reaction of Israel’s body politic to Palestinian citizens of Israel. This is what leading sociologist and researcher Honaida Ghanem calls Israel’s structural problem: its inability to reconcile that part of Israel’s political and leadership crisis is that in today’s Israel, anti-Arab sentiment is one of the few policies most Jewish Israelis can agree on, while they no longer agree on the nature of the state, the influence of religion over the state, or many other fundamental issues of identity and governance.

The prospect of a unity government with Eisenkot and Netanyahu remains possible, though not likely, primarily because of the personal and political risks such an unholy political marriage would entail for the change bloc leaders.

articles.title: Famine expect to rise due to global conflict, El Nino, warns UN
articles.excerpt:
Hunger ‌is set to worsen significantly in 16 global hotspots over the coming six ⁠months, mainly due to armed conflict and extreme climate events, two United Nations agencies said in a new report.

Th...
articles.body_text:
Hunger ‌is set to worsen significantly in 16 global hotspots over the coming six ⁠months, mainly due to armed conflict and extreme climate events, two United Nations agencies said in a new report.

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Friday that Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen ⁠faced the gravest threats of famine, driven by violence, displacement, economic hardship and extreme weather, including the El Nino phenomenon.

Listings in the report, released twice a year through the Global Network Against Food Crises, have risen from 13 hotspots in June, with ⁠Chad, Uganda and parts of both Southern Africa and Central America added, while Lebanon was removed.

Armed conflict and violence were driving hunger in 12 of the 16 hotspots, the report said, as soaring food, energy ⁠and transport costs were eroding people’s ability to feed themselves.

El Nino, which is set to intensify to exceptional levels in the coming months according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), is a major driver behind three of the four newly identified hotspots: Southern Africa, the Central American Dry Corridor and northeastern Uganda.

Covering December 2026 to May 2027, the agencies warned that shrinking humanitarian funding was affecting efforts to avert catastrophe.

In the five countries most at risk, all repeatedly cited on the hotspot list since 2022, humanitarian assistance has declined by nearly two-thirds over the 2022-2025 period, from $5.1bn to $2bn.

“While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” wrote the FAO and WFP.

While past humanitarian assistance helped avert famine, “the gains proved fragile and of limited duration: severe acute food insecurity risks – including risk of famine – re-emerged within a few years.”

In Sudan, famine remains a risk ⁠in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan through January 2027, as fighting disrupts food production, markets and aid deliveries.

The agencies also identified famine risks in parts of Somalia and South ‌Sudan, where escalating violence has compounded an already desperate humanitarian situation.

Afghanistan, Haiti, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Gaza were also classified as areas of very great concern.

Gaza was ‌downgraded ‌from the highest level of concern after small improvements in food security following the October 2025 “ceasefire”. But agencies warned that conditions remained fragile in Gaza, while in the occupied West Bank, acute food insecurity is expected to worsen.

articles.title: England’s Overton takes 5-12 as Australia bowled out for record low in T20
articles.excerpt:
Jamie Overton took a career-best 5-12 as England thrashed Australia by seven wickets in the third T20 international in Brisbane on Friday.

Overton’s figures were the best by an Englishman against Aus...
articles.body_text:
Jamie Overton took a career-best 5-12 as England thrashed Australia by seven wickets in the third T20 international in Brisbane on Friday.

Overton’s figures were the best by an Englishman against Australia in T20s as the home side were bundled out for 108, their lowest score on Australian soil.

“I thought Jamie Overton was outstanding tonight,” England captain Harry Brook said.

“He’s worked hard and put in some extra graft at training.

“He simplified his game and reaped the rewards tonight – he had it on a string and it felt like we could change the field and make them make a mistake.”

Brook won the toss and sent Australia in to bat, and off-spinner Liam Dawson struck early when he had Australian skipper Mitch Marsh caught at mid-on.

Jake Fraser-McGurk and Sam Harper attacked during the powerplay, taking the score to 55 after five overs.

Harper raced to 26 off 14 balls before Dawson grabbed his second when the Australian wicketkeeper got a top edge to Overton at mid-on.

Overton then swung into action with the ball, claiming the next five wickets as Australia slumped from 65-2 to 92-7 and then collapsed to 108 all out when Sam Curran clean-bowled Billy Stanlake.

Aneurin Donald, who smashed 85 off 32 on the Gold Coast on Tuesday, got the run chase off to a spectacular start, belting 31 from just 11 balls.

But a rain delay seemed to help the Australians, as Brook holed out for nine after play resumed, before Donald fell for 32, leaving England 49-3.

Another rain break threatened to stop England’s momentum again, but Jordan Cox blasted 33 in quick time to give the visitors an easy win and go ahead in the five-game series 2-1.

Marsh conceded that Australia were outplayed by a better team.

“No excuses, we’ve got to be better,” he said.

“We’ve all played Big Bash games here (at the Gabba).

“You have to give yourself the chance to cash in at the back end (of the innings), but we didn’t get near that tonight.”

The two teams head to Sydney for the fourth game on Sunday night.

articles.body_text:

It is Black Friday, but you can take a nice break from your shopping and watch another NFL game. I’m pretty pumped that we get this action. articles.title: From Hollywood mogul to Biden-Harris insiders, Democrats turn to familiar faces to shape their next chapter
articles.excerpt: National Review columnist Caroline Downey and Democratic strategist Al Mottur join 'The Faulkner Focus' to discuss Abdul El-Sayed's Senate victory in Michigan. The panel discusses Alexandria Ocasio-Co...
articles.body_text:
National Review columnist Caroline Downey and Democratic strategist Al Mottur join 'The Faulkner Focus' to discuss Abdul El-Sayed's Senate victory in Michigan. The panel discusses Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's rising influence and the impact on the 2028 Democratic primary.

On the heels of the blue wave in the 2026 U.S. midterms, incoming Democratic leaders are tapping an eclectic mix of political veterans, business executives and entertainment figures to help shape their transitions into power.

From a Hollywood mogul and former Biden administration officials to figures with ties to Republican leaders, the appointments offer an early glimpse into the people Democrats are turning to as they prepare to govern — and the experience and connections they hope to bring into their new administrations.

Several incoming Democrats are turning to familiar faces from the Biden administration. In New Mexico, Gov.-elect Deb Haaland tapped former Biden presidential speechwriter Felicia Salazar and former Interior Department official Joan Mooney for her transition team, while California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra selected Arsenio Mataka, who previously served as his senior counselor at the Department of Health and Human Services under Biden, to direct policy for his transition team. In Ohio, Democratic Gov.-elect Amy Acton tapped Elisabeth Hire, a former aide to then-Vice President Biden, as a transition co-chair.

Haaland's campaign and Becerra's campaign each did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

A sign points to a vote center during the in-person early voting period in California's Proposition 50 special election on Oct. 27, 2025 in West Hollywood, California. (Photo by Mario Tama/Getty Images)

The transition teams will help incoming leaders prepare to take office, including identifying potential administration officials, shaping policy priorities and laying the groundwork for their first days in power. The selections also offer a window into the experience, relationships and perspectives newly elected Democrats are turning to as they prepare to govern.

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, D-Mich., tapped Egyptian-American lawyer Brenda Abdelall as the director of his transition team, Politico Playbook first reported in early November. Abdelall previously claimed that Zionists were "controlling" much of U.S. politics, The Washington Free Beacon reported Nov. 6, though Harris' 2024 presidential campaign said at the time that the remarks did not reflect Abdelall's current views.

"The Zionists have a strong voice in American politics," Abdelall told the New York Sun during a conference for the American Muslim Council in 2002, the Free Beacon reported. "I would say they're controlling a lot of it."

Abdelall previously served as the assistant secretary of partnership and engagement at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. She also directed the Kamala Harris 2024 presidential campaign's outreach to Arab American voters, Reuters reported.

U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed speaks at the Michigan Democratic Party convention, on August 29, 2026, in Lansing, Michigan. (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News)

JEWISH LEADERS IN MICHIGAN PREPARE TO WORK WITH ABDUL EL-SAYED DESPITE LINGERING CONCERNS

El-Sayed campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner told Fox News Digital on Nov. 9 that Abdelall "comes to the role of transition director with decades of experience leading teams at the highest levels of politics, including the Biden-Harris administration."

"While at the Department of Homeland Security, Brenda worked to implement the nation’s first National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism and frequently spearheaded efforts to counter the rise of hate crimes and violence across the country," Richner added. "The transition team is committed to building a team that reflects the great diversity of Michigan and ensuring that the El-Sayed office serves all communities across the state."

El-Sayed is set to assume office on Jan. 3, 2027.

DEMOCRATIC SENATOR-ELECT CALLS TRUMP 'UNSERIOUS FOOL' WHILE DEFENDING COMBATIVE POLITICAL STYLE

Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, speaks at the Michigan Democratic Nominating Convention in Lansing, Mich., on Aug. 29, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

DEMOCRATS SEIZE MAJORITY OF GOVERNORS’ OFFICES IN ELECTION-NIGHT SHIFT

Democratic Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms announced Nov. 6 that filmmaker and actor Tyler Perry would serve as one of 10 co-chairs of her transition team, dubbed "Georgia's Promise," WBAL-TV reported. Perry has long been known for his philanthropic efforts, including supporting underserved communities and charitable causes across Georgia. Bottoms lauded Perry as "an entertainment mogul who is also a huge philanthropic part of our Georgia community and owns Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta," WDSU reported.

Victorious Georgia Democratic gubernatorial candidate, former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms, speaks onstage during her election night watch party at the Atlanta Marriott Marquis on Nov. 3, 2026 in Atlanta, Ga. (Megan Varner/Getty Images)

EX-BIDEN OFFICIAL WINS GEORGIA DEM PRIMARY FOR GOVERNOR IN BID TO END PARTY'S LOSING STREAK

The news that Perry will serve on Bottoms’ Georgia transition team has sparked some criticism due to the entertainment mogul facing two active lawsuits accusing him of sexual assault and misconduct, allegations his attorneys have denied, Variety reported Nov. 6.

Perry has denied all sexual assault and harassment allegations made against him, People reported on March 3.

Maxscene, a division of Tyler Perry Studios, did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Bottoms previously was an executive producer on Netflix’s "Miss Governor," a 2025 political comedy sitcom produced by Tyler Perry Studios, per online film database IMDb.

Other prominent figures that have been tapped for Bottoms' transition committee include Home Depot co-founder Arthur Blank and former CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance Roz Brewer, WBAL-TV reported.

Bottoms’ campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Bottoms is set to take office on Jan. 11, 2027.

Democratic Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson's transition team includes Mark Penley, a former deputy attorney general who reported outgoing Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton to the FBI, and Erin Epley, who served as lead attorney in Paxton's impeachment, The Houston Chronicle reported Nov. 16.

Johnson also tapped Amanda Crawford, a former appointee of Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, and Thaddeus Cleveland, a Republican sheriff from Terrell County, as part of his transition team, according to the Chronicle.

Johnson's campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Democratic Gov.-elect David Crowley is also turning to the world of professional sports, tapping Alex Lasry, a former senior vice president of the NBA's Milwaukee Bucks, to serve on his transition team, Wisconsin Public Radio reported Nov. 11.

Lasry, the son of former Bucks co-owner and billionaire businessman Marc Lasry, helped oversee the franchise's operations during its rise to the 2021 NBA championship and played a key role in developing Milwaukee's Fiserv Forum arena. He also mounted an unsuccessful bid for the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination in 2022.

Crowley's campaign did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.
