articles.title: Tributes flow for Molly Meldrum: Anthony Albanese, Jason Donovan and others remember music industry great
articles.excerpt:
Peter Andre, Richard Wilkins and Kate Ceberano share memories of ‘a truly unique character’ and ‘the fan all artists wish to have’

Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies...
articles.body_text:
Peter Andre, Richard Wilkins and Kate Ceberano share memories of ‘a truly unique character’ and ‘the fan all artists wish to have’

Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies aged 83

Friends and fans of Molly Meldrum have remembered the music industry great, who died on Monday at the age of 83.

Meldrum spent more than a decade hosting the ABC music show Countdown, leaving a lasting legacy on the Australian music landscape.

Anthony Albanese was among those paying tribute. “With an interview style that was inimitable and an enthusiasm that was uncontainable, Molly Meldrum loved music almost as much as we loved him,” the wrote in a post on X.

“On Countdown and beyond, he championed Australian artists and brought international acts to our shores. He gave new artists a leg up and established artists a welcoming embrace. And over the years as he implored us to do ourselves a favour, he became a central part of the Australian soundtrack. We were lucky to have him. May Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum rest in peace.”

Jason Donovan said Meldrum was the “very heart” of the music program while he was growing up, calling the man a “truly unique character, a great Australian and one of this country’s greatest pioneers and ambassadors for music and entertainment”.

“He was loved, recognised and respected around the world for the extraordinary contribution he made to Australian music and the artists he championed,” Donovan wrote on Facebook. “There will never be another quite like him.”

The former Neighbours star shared a memory of Meldrum appearing on an episode alongside Kylie Minogue and Guy Pearce, adding: “What a day that was!”

The television presenter Richard Wilkins remembered his longtime friend on-air on Monday morning. The pair used to travel around the world for interviews, Wilkins said, which led to great memories and hilarious stories.

“Australian music would not be Australian music without Molly’s incredible contribution,” Wilkins said. “I shared so many overseas trips with Molly, which was a joy and a curse. He lost 13 passports, that was the tally I got to.

“We went from a Michael Jackson gig in Munich to see Bruce Springsteen in Paris. That was the sort of thing we used to get up to back in the day.”

Gavin Wood, a longtime friend of Meldrum’s who worked on Countdown, said the host was “one of the craziest, most colourful, funniest and most beautiful people you could ever have the pleasure of meeting”.

“What he has done for the Australian music industry is simply phenomenal,” Wood wrote. “His contribution, passion, enthusiasm and unwavering commitment to Australian artists helped shape an entire generation of music and entertainment.

“There will never be another Molly Meldrum. You simply cannot measure anyone against him.”

Bands and artists echoed those sentiments.

Meldrum produced Russell Morris’s 1969 single the Real Thing, which reached #1 on the charts. “He was a unique, and loveable individual,” Morris wrote on Facebook. “I was lucky enough to call him my friend, and mentor. The journey we went on was pretty surreal – his creative energy and insights were exceptional … He achieved things that were truly great. Things that sometimes seemed impossible.”

“He was such a huge presence in the Australian music industry and was a great friend and supporter of so many up and coming bands and artists – ourselves included,” the band Human Nature wrote. “Thanks for everything Molly. Rest easy.”

The singer Peter Andre posted a photo with Meldrum, praising him for helping to elevate his career and saying “this really hurts”.

“If it wasn’t for this man, I would not of had any of the chances I had to make it in any way in the entertainment industry back when it was near impossible to get noticed,” Andre wrote. “He believed in me from day one and I am forever grateful to Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum.”

Kate Ceberano wrote: “He had no agenda he wanted, no praise, he never basked in any reflected glory or self pride. He simply wanted the world to hear what he could hear, wanted you to see what he was looking at and then blow it up to 11. Way up sky high. No dream is too big. No cringe, withholding nothing.

“He was the fan all artists wish to have.”

Iva Davies of Icehouse also paid tribute: “He was such a bright, larger than life figure in our Australian music scene for so many years … Like the rest of the music community that owed so much to his support, the band and I are so thankful that Molly was a part of our lives and music. There will never be another like him and he will be sorely missed by so many.”

The Australian Recording Industry Association issued its own praise of Meldrum’s work, noting that both he and the Countdown program were the first inductees into the Aria Hall of Fame who weren’t recording artists, back in 2014.

“It is impossible to imagine what Australian music would look like without Molly’s long and storied career,” said Annabelle Herd, Aria’s chief executive. “He shaped the music taste of a generation of Australians and gave so much of himself for the good of Australian artists, for which our whole industry is eternally grateful.”

The St Kilda football club remembered Meldrum as a “lifelong Sainter”, saying the organisation was deeply saddened by his death.

“An iconic and passionate supporter of our football club, Molly changed and brightened the lives of so many across a storied career,” the club wrote on Facebook.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon ‘executed’ Jesse Baird and Luke Davies then lied about it, prosecution argues
articles.excerpt:
Crown urges jury to reject accused’s claim of self-defence and find him guilty of murdering Sydney couple

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free...
articles.body_text:
Crown urges jury to reject accused’s claim of self-defence and find him guilty of murdering Sydney couple

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon is a “proven and persistent liar” and the evidence in his double murder trial shows the deaths of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies could only have been an “execution”, a court has been told.

Lamarre-Condon is accused of fatally shooting the Sydney couple with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.

The former officer has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter, claiming the two men died while he acted in “self-defence”.

Crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC urged the jury to reject Lamarre-Condon’s account and convict him on all three counts, as he wrapped up his closing statement on Monday.

Driven by his jealous obsession, the accused drove to Paddington in a hired car, waited for his opportunity, entered the house with a gun loaded with stolen bullets, and shot Baird in the back and temple, Hatfield alleged.

“It was not self-defence or an accident,” he told the New South Wales supreme court.

“The evidence speaks only to an execution.”

Lamarre-Condon had testified he shot Baird after he lunged at him with a knife.

During this struggle, his gun was then flung across the room and picked up by Davies before the officer grabbed his arm and pushed the gun towards Davies.

Davies then pulled the trigger and shot himself, Lamarre-Condon told the court.

But this defence rests entirely on his own account and even if Baird had picked up a knife, it would not have assisted him against a glock, Hatfield said.

“You might think he is a proven and persistent liar and such a scenario is completely contrary to the weight of the evidence,” he told the court.

“The accused’s account is not the truth. It is a story made up after the fact in an attempt to meet the evidence.”

The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: US army to blow up bomb-making chemicals despite safety concerns
articles.excerpt:
Army invokes emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid court order despite worries about health and environment risks

The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that had put ...
articles.body_text:
Army invokes emergency provisions in Iowa to avoid court order despite worries about health and environment risks

The US army plans to invoke emergency provisions to avoid a court order that had put on hold plans to detonate several tons of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa, saying that continued delays will make it more dangerous as the weather starts to turn colder.

“To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action,” government lawyers told the eight US circuit court of appeals in a filing late on Saturday. “Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay.”

The army plans to detonate the chemicals by Tuesday.

Environmental groups criticized the government’s move, decrying it as a maneuver to get around a court order and avoid public demands for safety and transparency.

The appeals court on Thursday granted a request by environmentalists to put on hold a permit that cleared the way for the detonation in Middletown, a small community about 160 miles (257km) south-east of Des Moines. It was initially planned for Friday, but the army later announced that it would push the operation to Monday after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.

Environmentalists have called for a review of the emergency permit that was approved earlier this month by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

In a statement on Sunday, the Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice questioned claims that all alternatives were given appropriate consideration.

“The Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm,” said Thien Chau, an attorney at Earthjustice.

Government lawyers said the army doesn’t need a permit to take emergency action against an immediate threat from explosive material.

They said the standards of a federal law regulating hazardous waste don’t apply in situations when there is an immediate threat to health, safety or the environment as determined by an explosive or munitions emergency response specialist.

Officials contend that the chemicals are unstable, and the risk of an uncontrolled explosion is growing, particularly as temperatures drop. They said there is a risk that the chemicals may explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30F (-1C) in the coming days.

In March, staff at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant found several dozen barrels of degraded lead azide, which is used in munitions production. Crystallization of the material created an unstable and dangerous situation, prompting the army to assemble experts in munitions chemistry, engineering and environmental safety to come up with a plan.

According to EPA documents, alternatives such as neutralizing and decomposing the drums’ contents with other chemicals were considered. But officials said handling the drums would increase the probability of an accidental, fatal detonation.

The environmental groups disagreed, arguing in their petition that other alternatives were not fully considered. They also criticized officials for not sharing more information with the public.

Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but thousands more in surrounding areas could be affected by detonated material that could disperse in the air and land on the ground.

Iowans in the region were told to stay inside, keep windows and doors closed, bring pets and livestock indoors, and clean cars, windowsills and outdoor surfaces after.

“The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground,” an advisory states. “Lead is toxic to humans and animals.”

articles.title: WHO chief calls for peace amid heavy fighting in Ebola-hit DR Congo region
articles.excerpt:
The World ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Health Organization (WHO) chief has urged peace following heavy fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) northeastern province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

...
articles.body_text:
The World ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Health Organization (WHO) chief has urged peace following heavy fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) northeastern province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠on ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Sunday that fighting near a hospital in the DRC’s Ituri ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠province disrupted Ebola response efforts and forced health workers and aid partners to shelter ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠inside a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.

“Heavy fighting has been ongoing since yesterday in the vicinity of a hospital in Ituri – in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged,” Tedros said on X.

“The situation has disrupted the work of the hospital and the wider Ebola response, putting patients, families and health workers at grave risk.”

Medical staff have been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward in the facility for more than 24 hours, and the WHO is working to arrange a safe exit for the team and “for the hospital facilities, staff and patients to be protected,” Tedros also said.

As of November 17, the WHO reported a total of 5,678 deaths out of 11,613 cases in the DRC, the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country.

The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that “while some areas had seen a slight decline in cases, sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the country.”

Ituri and North Kivu, in the eastern part of the DRC, remain the most affected provinces.

The virus, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids, has spread across swaths of the DRC’s east and northeast, which have been plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

Earlier in November, armed men thought to be linked to an ISIL (ISIS)-affiliated group raided villages and killed dozens of people in North Kivu, forcing ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠patients with confirmed and suspected Ebola infections to flee.

The outbreak is also occurring amid ongoing fighting between government forces and the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, which has seized key cities in eastern DRC, making transport of healthcare resources to remote regions difficult.

articles.title: Trump hosts third crypto gala for meme coin amid conflict of interest outcry
articles.excerpt:
Virginia dinner comes as Democrats accuse president of improperly profiting from his cryptocurrency ventures

Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on ⁠Sunday night at hi...
articles.body_text:
Virginia dinner comes as Democrats accuse president of improperly profiting from his cryptocurrency ventures

Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on ⁠Sunday night at his ​country club in Virginia, rewarding top holders of his own meme coin as Democrats accuse the president of improperly profiting from his crypto ventures.

The dinner, set to take place at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, will include meet-and-greets with Trump supporters including the boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O’Leary, NBA champion Tristan Thompson and mentalist Lior Suchard, according to the event’s website.

The gala’s access and perks are divided by tiers for the 185 holders of $TRUMP, the president’s meme coin. A Trump fragrance, a poster, a “commemorative” ticket, and a “Trump watch” are reserved for 120 attendees. Meanwhile, the top 29 investors are invited to a VIP reception, and the top four will receive a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch”.

Trump has hosted two similar galas since he took office last year, bringing a flurry of criticism as Democrats accuse Trump and his family of monetizing his brand through an array of equities and crypto ventures while in office.

After sweepingwins in the midterms, Democrats have vowed to investigate conflicts of interest involving Trump and his personal wealth during his presidency. They also say they plan to push for legislation that would ban activities such as the meme coin gala dinner.

“This dinner and scoring mechanism appear carefully constructed to increase investment in $TRUMP, allowing the President to abuse the power of his office to personally enrich himself, as he has throughout this term,” reads a letter sent by Adam Schiff and eight other US senators last month.

Since returning to the White House, Trump has made more than $1bn from his crypto businesses, according to financial disclosures released in June. Trump received more than $500m from his World Liberty Financial business selling new crypto products, and raked another $600m from sales of souvenir-type “meme” coins stamped with Trump’s face. Trump launched his $Trump meme coin days before his inauguration.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Interest in the $TRUMP coin dinner has plummeted, with contestants’ combined holdings dropping from $148m in May 2025 to $8.6m in this month’s gala.

More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they ‌are linked to foreign nationals, according to an analysis of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, non-profit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.

“Neither the President nor his family ⁠has ever engaged — or will ever engage — in conflicts of interest,” White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters ​earlier this year. “President Trump proudly made ​the United States the crypto capital of the world ​through executive actions.“

The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record ​lows. Together, outside investors in their ‌five main crypto and ​crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5bn​, according to a Reuters analysis.

The Trump meme coin has earned the Trump family at least $635m, according to the president’s June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3bn through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.

The president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430m.

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo doubles down on call to oust Schumer over 'entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties'
articles.excerpt: Actor Mark Ruffalo face backlash over his posts attacking Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for following "entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties." (Karwai Tang/WireImage via Getty Images; Alex Wong/Get...
articles.body_text:
Actor Mark Ruffalo face backlash over his posts attacking Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for following "entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties." (Karwai Tang/WireImage via Getty Images; Alex Wong/Getty Images)

Actor Mark Ruffalo said Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., was too beholden to "entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties" to lead the Senate in a post on X, advocating for Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., as Senate majority leader.

"Israel is just one issue in a whole host of reasons Van Hollen is the right leader for our times. We need Justice, we need leadership that follows the will of the people not entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties," Ruffalo wrote on X. "Does not follow entrenched fossil fuel and corporate interests, nor throws a blind eye to the hard realties [sic] we face today."

The four-time Academy Award nominee argued that Van Hollen had the integrity, strength and spirit to fight "the social and moral corruption that has set in with age-old presumptions" in the incoming Democratic-led Congress.

BILL MAHER BLASTS DEMOCRATIC PARTY, SAYS IT IS FINE WITH RELIGION 'AS LONG AS THAT FAITH ISN’T JEWISH'

Mark Ruffalo faced backlash over his criticism of Sen. Chuck Schumer on X over the weekend. (Hoda Davaine/Getty Images)

"We have absolutely nothing to lose by replacing Sen. Schumer," Ruffalo wrote. "We can only gain more justice and freedom. Put pressure on your senators. Now is the time. Keep the momentum of this election going. Thank you, Senator Schumer, but it’s time to move aside."

Ruffalo faced backlash across both sides of the political aisle for what critics viewed as a slight against Schumer's Jewish background.

"Entrenched religious beliefs? Entrenched loyalties? Please elaborate, @MarkRuffalo," Anti-Defamation League CEO and National Director Jonathan Greenblatt wrote. "Which religion? Loyal to whom?"

"There are many devout Senators & Congressmen with 'entrenched religious beliefs.' Chuck Schumer is not one of them," Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, wrote. "Van Hollen is far more tied to the Episcopal Bishop of Washington than Schumer is to any leading Rabbi. Guess what really bothers Ruffalo."

RABBINIC GROUP ACCUSES JEWISH ENTERTAINERS OF 'WHITEWASHING ANTISEMITISM' IN MARK RUFFALO DEFENSE

"Can you clarify what you mean by 'entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties'?" political commentator Meghan McCain asked.

By Sunday, Ruffalo doubled down on his post, citing Schumer's 2018 comments at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) annual policy conference where he was quoted saying, "Of course, we say it’s our land, the Torah says it, but they don’t believe in the Torah. So that’s the reason there is not peace."

"These are Senator Schumer’s words, not mine," Ruffalo added on X.

Critics accused Mark Ruffalo of invoking Sen. Schumer's Jewish background in his attack against the Senate minority leader. (Alex Wroblewski / AFP via Getty Images)

"Schumer is entitled to his religious beliefs, but those beliefs cannot determine the rights of another people. And they certainly cannot substitute for international law," Ruffalo continued. "This is a conflict about land, freedom, security, equality and self-determination. Peace requires justice, accountability and respect for the rights of both Palestinians and Israelis."

Fox News Digital reached out to Ruffalo's representative and Schumer's office for comment.

MORE THAN 180 JEWISH ENTERTAINERS RALLY BEHIND ACTOR MARK RUFFALO IN PROTEST LETTER

Human rights attorney Brooke Goldstein, executive director of The Lawfare Project and Founder of the #EndJewHatred movement, denounced Ruffalo's posts, calling the actor "obsessively fixated" on the Jewish state to the point of questioning members of the party he supports.

"And now they’re even turning on one of their own, Senator Chuck Schumer, because apparently even being a loyal Democrat isn’t enough when you’re Jewish," Goldstein told Fox News Digital. "They’re saying the quiet part out loud now, no longer afraid to invoke his Jewish identity as grounds for distrust. The message is unmistakable: ‘He’s a Jew. We can’t trust him.'"

"His [Ruffalo's] obsessive fixation on the Jewish state, his selective outrage, and his breathtaking moral relativism raise serious questions about whether his "so called activism" is driven by genuine concern for America’s interests or by hostility toward Jews," she added.

Mark Ruffalo faced accusations of antisemitism over his attacks on the Paramount merger. (Lia Toby/Getty Images)

Ruffalo previously faced accusations of antisemitism after he criticized the Paramount merger earlier this year, focusing on CEO David Ellison and his father's history of supporting Israel.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Molly Meldrum, Countdown host and promoter of Australian music, dies aged 83
articles.excerpt:
Much-loved broadcaster played a critical role in exposing rest of the world to Australian music – and vice versa

Tributes flow for Molly Meldrum: Human Nature, Jason Donovan and others remember music...
articles.body_text:
Much-loved broadcaster played a critical role in exposing rest of the world to Australian music – and vice versa

Tributes flow for Molly Meldrum: Human Nature, Jason Donovan and others remember music industry great

Molly Meldrum, the Australian music journalist, broadcaster and producer, has died at the age of 83.

He died peacefully in the early hours of Monday morning at a hospital in Melbourne, his longtime friend and manager, Mark Klemens, confirmed to the Guardian.

“We have lost a true Australian icon, a man who opened doors for so many and entertained millions of people here and around the world,” Klemens said.

“He was unconventional and wonderfully unpredictable, but always caring, always funny and always down to earth, with a passion the rest of us could only envy. He made the most of his life, and boy, was it a full one. Rest in peace, Molly.”

Meldrum’s partner, Yan Wongngam, and family said in a statement issued by Klemens: “Affectionately dubbed ‘the Guru’, Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music. He shaped not only the sound of a nation but also the dreams of generations who grew up with his voice guiding them..

“Yan cared for Molly with great love and devotion, especially through his final years. The family is deeply grateful to him, to Molly’s many loyal friends, and to the staff at Epworth Richmond for their wonderful care.”

The Stetson-wearing Countdown presenter is credited with engineering the breakthrough of Abba, Blondie and Madonna in Australia. During his time on the wildly popular Sunday evening ABC music show from 1974 to 1987, he championed songs including Blondie’s In the Flesh, John Mellencamp’s I Need a Lover, Duran Duran’s Planet Earth and Madonna’s Holiday, transforming then unknown tracks into Top 10 hits in Australia.

Meldrum also passionately promoted Australian performers, giving exposure on Countdown to dozens who went on to local or international fame, including INXS, Kylie Minogue, Skyhooks and Mental as Anything.

In a post on X, the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, paid tribute to Meldrum: “With an interview style that was inimitable and an enthusiasm that was uncontainable, Molly Meldrum loved music almost as much as we loved him. On Countdown and beyond, he championed Australian artists and brought international acts to our shores. He gave new artists a leg up and established artists a welcoming embrace. And over the years as he implored us to do ourselves a favour, he became a central part of the Australian soundtrack. We were lucky to have him.”

Victorian Premier Ben Carroll said Meldrum will be given a state funeral. “All of our thoughts as Victorians and indeed Australians are with Molly Meldrum’s family and his friends, and we know how wide that network was,” he said.

Elton John once described Meldrum as the “single most important influence in Australian pop music”.

Meldrum never disguised his unabashed fervour as a fan, even while forming decades-long friendships with an array of global stars.

He developed an obsession with the Beatles after their explosion on to the world stage, and eventually interviewed his pop idol, John Lennon, who fed him the scoop of the band’s impending break-up. But Meldrum did nothing with the incendiary information because he “was so in awe” of Lennon.

Born Ian Meldrum in Orbost, Victoria, to a family he called “quite dysfunctional”, the larger-than-life character moved to live with an aunt and uncle in Shepparton from the age of 12. He went from wanting to be a conductor to becoming entranced with the idea of producing music and later lived with the family of his close friend, the singer Ronnie Burns.

He was one of the first openly gay personalities on Australian television and was known for his bumbling interview technique and for his chaotic and colourful scuffles. On the 40th anniversary of Countdown in 2014, Prince Charles recalled a shambolic 1977 interview with Meldrum, telling the ABC: “There is an old show business saying which warns never to work with animals or children, but nobody prepared me for Molly Meldrum.”

Meldrum began appearing on camera on Countdown in mid-1975, delivering the weekly Rock Report, redubbed Humdrum by a guest host, John Paul Young. While reviewing albums, Meldrum would often hold LPs up awkwardly, making them hard to see under the glare of stage lights. ABC policy prohibited hosts endorsing products, so “do yourself a favour” became Meldrum’s catchphrase.

In the 1980s Meldrum landed various presenting gigs on television: the 1985 Oz for Africa concert, the Australian leg of Live Aid; the ABC interview show The Meldrum Tapes and a regular music segment, Molly’s Melodrama, on the variety show Hey Hey It’s Saturday.

In 2011 Meldrum fell from a ladder in the back yard of his Melbourne home and was placed in intensive care in a critical condition, undergoing surgery for head and spinal injuries. After four months he recovered enough to begin appearing in public again.

In 1986 he was made a member of the Order of Australia, with a citation for “service to the fostering of international relief and to youth”. In 2012 he was inducted into the Logie Hall of Fame. In 2014, when Meldrum became the first non-recording artist to be inducted into the Aria Hall of Fame, Minogue said the Australian music industry was “blessed to have had you in our lives for over four decades”.

Elton John was similarly unreserved in his praise, saying in 2019: “I don’t think anyone has done more for music in Australia than Molly Meldrum.”

Meldrum is survived by his partner, Yan Wongngam, his adopted son and his two younger brothers.

articles.title: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
articles.excerpt:
Asian stock markets have opened to sharp losses amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom.

Key indexes in South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong fell on Monday, continuing Friday’s tec...
articles.body_text:
Asian stock markets have opened to sharp losses amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom.

Key indexes in South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong fell on Monday, continuing Friday’s tech-led sell-off on both sides of the Pacific.

The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi) fell as much as 4.3 percent in early trading, while the Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Stock Index (Taiex) and the Hang Seng Index both dipped more than 1 percent.

Japan’s stock markets were closed for Labour Thanksgiving Day.

On Friday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 closed 3.7 percent lower for its seventh straight loss, while the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3 percent to erase all of its gains for 2026, following a rout in Asia.

The Kospi, Nikkei 225, and the Taiex entered the weekend between 5.1 percent and 6.2 percent lower, while the Hang Seng Index finished down 1.9 percent.

Investors have long been concerned that tech firms may not be able to sustain the multi-trillion-dollar investments they have poured into the infrastructure needed to train and run AI.

Global AI-related investment, much of it fuelled by debt, is expected to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.

Concerns that the AI boom may be running out of steam have been exacerbated by growing calls for greater oversight of the sector.

The Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the US midterm elections is expected to slow data centre construction in US states, while the alleged espionage scandal embroiling chip giant Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang has led to a push for tighter restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips.

articles.title: Urgent warning issued to cruise passengers about strict new law in Mexico
articles.excerpt:
Clint Henderson, managing editor at The Points Guy, explains why cruise costs are climbing and why sailing can still offer vacationers good value.

Cruise passengers are being warned they may need to ...
articles.body_text:
Clint Henderson, managing editor at The Points Guy, explains why cruise costs are climbing and why sailing can still offer vacationers good value.

Cruise passengers are being warned they may need to provide extensive documentation for onshore activities at ports in Mexico.

The sweeping law now requires adults traveling to Mexico with minors to prove their relationship to the children in the group, or face denial of service at hotels, resorts and tours, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported.

Effective Nov. 14, 2026, an amendment to Mexico's General Tourism Law places pressure on tourism providers to verify family relationships, according to Travel Market Report.

CRUISE TIPPING CHARGES ARE 'OUT OF CONTROL' SAY PASSENGERS AS COMPANIES TOUT 'EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE'

The Mexican Senate unanimously passed the measure to combat child trafficking and exploitation, aiming to shed the country's status as a major destination for such crimes.

"Pedophiles don't come to Mexico by chance," noted Sen. Laura Esquivel Torres, as reported by the same blog.

A change to Mexico's General Tourism Law places pressure on tourism providers to verify family relationships. Pictured here, Carnival cruise passengers disembark at Costa Maya Cruise Port in Mexico. (iStock)

"Starting today, we will begin to shut down these opportunities," Torres added.

Fox News Digital reached out to Sen. Torres and Royal Caribbean for additional information.

POPULAR CRUISE LINE'S BIKINI CRACKDOWN COULD SURPRISE PASSENGERS AT ISLAND PORTS

Tourism operators are legally required to check documents and must notify authorities if an adult cannot prove legal guardianship or parentage, according to news outlet TravelHost.

Travelers should be prepared to present passports, long-form birth certificates and custody or guardianship paperwork, the same blog noted.

When cruisers in Mexico, pictured here, disembark at a port, they are required to bring documentation proving minors are related to parents. (iStock)

Documentation explaining any differing last names between a parent and child is also recommended.

Even if cruise passengers are only stopping in a Mexican port for the day, the rules apply to all local services.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

While simply disembarking from a cruise ship might not trigger a document check, booking a beach club day pass, a local snorkeling excursion or renting a vacation home likely will, the blog reported (it is not affiliated with Royal Caribbean).

When walking around shops in Costa Maya, Mexico, families must bring documentation explaining differing last names between a parent and child. (iStock)

Travelers are urged to call hotels and tour operators in advance to confirm paperwork requirements.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The Mexican government has not yet released an official checklist, but travel experts advise bringing a folder with these documents, according to the same blog:

Travelers have been taking to Reddit to weigh in on the new rules.

"This is going to be a mess," one person wrote.

"There has been no formal guidance given by the Mexican government on what will be accepted and different hotels (including different people at the same hotel) have been giving different answers," the same commenter added.

Royal Caribbean passengers disembarking from the Oasis of the Seas, pictured here, will require documentation for minors in Cozumel, Mexico. (iStock)

"Bring all government docs and letters from parent authorizing you to have [temporary] guardianship of their kids for travel," another Reddit user said. "Not that hard, really."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I own a travel agency and [before that] was a Spanish teacher for 17 years. [I] traveled to Mexico with my students every summer and I always had a form for this — they used to often check," a third Reddit user said.

Cruise passengers on the Norwegian Joy cruise ship, pictured above, in Costa Maya, Mexico, will need documentation for minors. (Jeff Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Another chimed in, "My only issue with using the birth [certificate] proof is that a passport and birth certificate are often the only, or certainly the two most important identity documents, a child has. Having both lost or stolen while out of the country would be very stressful to deal with."

"I also don’t understand why it matters for hotels," the Reddit user added.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Mexican Embassy in the United States, Mexico's Secretariat of Tourism and World Vision Mexico for more information.

Jessica Mekles is an editor on the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Cameroon’s ex-rebels caught between hiding and broken promises
articles.excerpt: Douala, Cameroon – Collins Mbah says he hunted down and killed several Cameroonian soldiers in the English-speaking Northwest region during his time as a separatist fighter between 2016 and 2020. Toda...
articles.body_text:
Douala, Cameroon – Collins Mbah says he hunted down and killed several Cameroonian soldiers in the English-speaking Northwest region during his time as a separatist fighter between 2016 and 2020. Today, in the coastal city of Douala, the man in his mid-30s, who went by the name Commander No Sorrow, has taken on a different role: traditional healer, tending to lives rather than taking them.

Mbah says he abandoned the armed struggle after realising that fellow fighters were turning against the very people they had set out to protect. But he has firmly ruled out joining the government’s disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration (DDR) programme.

“Quitting the struggle and joining the government disarmament programme would have meant I betrayed the people,” said Mbah, who dropped out of secondary school to join the revolt. “I don’t want to have anything to do with the government or the struggle any more. All I need now is peace of mind,” he told Al Jazeera.

October marked a decade since protests erupted in Cameroon’s English-speaking Northwest and Southwest regions, eventually escalating into an armed conflict between separatist fighters and government forces.

The unrest began in late 2016 after Anglophone lawyers and teachers protested against the appointment of Francophone magistrates unfamiliar with British common law to courts in English-speaking regions, and French-speaking teachers unable to communicate fluently in English to schools there. The protests were met with a government crackdown and eventually gave rise to a separatist movement seeking independence for the two regions, which its supporters call “Ambazonia”.

The conflict has killed thousands of people, displaced hundreds of thousands and disrupted education across the two English-speaking regions, according to humanitarian and human rights organisations. New figures released in October by the Cameroonian nonprofit Centre for Human Rights and Democracy in Africa (CHRDA) suggest the death toll could be as high as 10,000.

The fighting remains deadlocked, with separatist groups continuing attacks and kidnappings while the government pursues a military campaign. Alongside its military operations, the government has launched a community dialogue initiative, after distancing itself from Swiss- and Canadian-supported peace efforts.

Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngute launched the initiative in Buea, the capital of Southwest, in September and in Bamenda, the capital of the Northwest, on October 15. Local leaders are being encouraged to persuade fighters to surrender and enter DDR centres. At the two events, 55 fighters – 25 in the Southwest and 30 in the Northwest – were presented as having renounced the armed struggle.

Despite leaving the rebellion, Mbah says he remains on the government’s wanted list. Without a national identity card, the father of three struggles to move freely around Douala and occasionally ventures into the outskirts to collect traditional herbs.

“I was initiated into traditional healing during childhood. The amulets and concoctions helped me foresee any danger when I was on the war front. Today, I use the same to heal,” he said. “But I don’t stay in a particular neighbourhood for long – I always move to the next to avoid being caught.”

Mbah is among former fighters who have chosen to reintegrate into society independently rather than enter government-run rehabilitation centres. Many say they fear arrest or poor treatment if they surrender.

Peter Mosongo, 28, now works as a motorcycle taxi rider in Buea after leaving the struggle in 2019. He joined in 2018 to protect his family but quit after witnessing what he describes as the indiscriminate killing of civilians by fellow fighters.

“I received threats from the fighters when I quit. They even kidnapped my father to force him to produce me,” Mosongo said. “I didn’t join DDR upon quitting out of fear that I may end up in prison. It was also being rumoured that those who surrendered were being killed silently.”

Mosongo says he also lost two cousins to the conflict.

Another former fighter, Richard Bende, left in 2019 because he believed the rebellion had become a “scores-settling venture”. He had fought government soldiers in Bamusso, in the Southwest, and now works as a secondary school history and geography teacher. Like Mbah and Mosongo, he avoided the DDR programme, citing concerns about the treatment of former fighters at its centres.

Paul Mukete, who fought in Kumba from 2017 to 2020 under the nickname King of Vultures, chose a different path. But six years after entering the DDR programme in Tiko town, in the Southwest, he says he has little to show for it.

Apart from learning poultry and pig farming, Mukete says he has received no psychological care.

“We gave intelligence information to the military, who used it to kill some separatist fighters who refused to lay down their weapons,” he said. “We were about 600 in the DDR centre, but many have since left out of frustration. Some even rejoined the struggle and got killed.”

The 29-year-old father of three now takes on odd jobs to support his family.

His account raises questions about whether the programme is providing former fighters with the support they need to rebuild their lives and remain out of the conflict.

Fonbeh Hedwick Chia, a mental health specialist and founder of the Bamenda-based Living Vine Mental Health Services, says both fighters and civilians in the English-speaking regions have been exposed to psychological trauma.

He argues that the DDR centres lack the therapeutic support needed to rehabilitate former fighters, estimating that about 800 have renounced the armed struggle.

“The government is more concerned with the propaganda made when they come to the DDR than their integral welfare,” Chia told Al Jazeera, arguing that former fighters need psychological care to address the trauma of atrocities committed and witnessed during the conflict.

Without proper rehabilitation, he warns, former fighters risk remaining marginalised and could become a source of further instability.

The accounts of former fighters and Chia’s assessment point to a central challenge for the DDR programme: persuading rebels to surrender is only the first step, while helping them return to civilian life requires sustained support.

Cameroon’s Anglophone crisis has roots in its colonial past. Initially colonised by Germany in 1884, the territory was divided between Britain and France after World War I.

French Cameroon gained independence in 1960. In 1961, British-administered Southern Cameroons voted in a United Nations-organised plebiscite to join the independent Republic of Cameroon, forming a federal state. The arrangement was dissolved in 1972 following a controversial referendum, ending the Anglophone regions’ federal status.

Unlike some conflicts involving more centralised rebel movements, Cameroon’s separatist rebellion has no single command structure. Dozens of smaller factions operate across Northwest and Southwest, with some receiving financial support and weapons from diaspora groups.

The prolonged fighting has brought human rights abuses by both government forces and separatists. Some armed groups have also shifted towards criminal activities, including kidnapping for ransom.

Chris Roberts, a political scientist at the University of Calgary in Canada, says the conflict is rooted less in language differences than in “decades of poor governance from a political system that has kept the same president in power since 1982”.

Although the government has repeatedly claimed the war is over, Roberts says continued firefights, ambushes and attacks demonstrate otherwise.

He argues that political reform in Yaoundé is essential to ending the conflict. He describes the October 2025 presidential election as “strategically rigged” and argues that it offers little prospect of resolving the crisis. A future presidential succession crisis could create opportunities for reform but also risk destabilising the country.

“There will not be a military solution to this war,” Roberts said.

articles.body_text:
"Yes Dear" star Anthony Clark died on Tuesday, Nov. 10. He was 62. (Getty Images)

Anthony Clark's official cause of death was due to septic shock, according to a death certificate obtained by People magazine. He was 62.

The "Yes, Dear" star died on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Influenza A and chronic alcoholism were included as underlying conditions, the outlet reported.

In addition, acute kidney failure was listed as a significant contributing factor in Clark's death.

'YES, DEAR' STAR ANTHONY CLARK DEAD AT 62

Anthony Clark's cause of death was revealed to be due to septic shock. (Getty Images)

"Anthony was one of the funniest and most talented comedians and actors I have ever had the pleasure of watching," his longtime manager, Barry Katz, told Fox News Digital.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"It was an honor to represent him and he will be missed for the joy, happiness, and love he brought to everyone he worked with and the audiences that were blessed to see his undeniable performances."

Clark's "Yes, Dear" co-star, Mike O'Malley, initially shared the news of his death in a tribute posted on X. Deadline then reported that Clark died of "complications related to pneumonia and the flu."

Anthony Clark starred alongside Jean Louisa Kelly and Mike O'Malley in "Yes, Dear." (CBS via Getty Images)

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Anthony Clark died yesterday. He was a hilarious guy," O'Malley wrote. "When my wife Lisa and I were dating back in the mid-nineties, Anthony was already famous in Boston, regularly selling out comedy shows. The first time we saw him at The Comedy Connection, we laughed and laughed and laughed.

STACY KEACH DEAD AT 85 AS ‘MIKE HAMMER’ STAR’S WIFE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE

"He was so unique — one of those comics who is laughing along with you at the absurdity of his stories and observations. I was a fan before I was a friend. We spoke on the phone three weeks ago. He had us laughing loudly once again. Attached are some snapshots from our last episode of Yes Dear, which ended 20 years ago after 122 episodes. Rest in peace. Tony."

Born in 1964, the Virginia native kickstarted his career in comedy at an early age. In 1986, Clark, who graduated from Emerson College with a mass communication degree, won a national college comedy award.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Clark starred in NBC’s "Boston Common" from 1996 to 1997, followed by "Soul Man" opposite Dan Aykroyd. His biggest success, however, came with "Yes, Dear," which ran from 2000 to 2006 alongside O’Malley, Jean Louisa Kelly and Liza Snyder.

His film credits include "Dogfight," "The Thing Called Love" and "The Rock." He also appeared on "Ellen" and hosted the fourth season of "Last Comic Standing" in 2006.

Fox News Digital's Christina Dugan-Ramirez contributed to this report.

Tracy Wright is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital. Send story tips to Tracy.Wright@fox.com.

articles.title: Chiefs and Bills take care of business ahead of the NFL’s biggest regular-season game
articles.excerpt:
Craig Carton is LOVING watching the downfall of the New England Patriots.

Sunday in the NFL felt a little like November in the SEC for the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills. You know how SEC teams...
articles.body_text:
Craig Carton is LOVING watching the downfall of the New England Patriots.

Sunday in the NFL felt a little like November in the SEC for the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills. You know how SEC teams like to schedule a late-season cupcake as a tune-up before the big rivalry game? Well, the Chiefs and Bills don’t get to pick their opponents, but whoever put together the Week 11 schedule did them both a favor.

When I wrote about the Week 11 betting lines Thursday, Buffalo was favored by 16.5 points and Kansas City by 15.5. Both covered those numbers. The Bills beat the Miami Dolphins, 26-9, while the Chiefs demolished the Arizona Cardinals, 34-7.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Of course, the analogy only works if the cupcake leads into a big rivalry game. And that’s exactly what’s in store for NFL fans on Thanksgiving night, when Patrick Mahomes and the 8-2 Chiefs head to Buffalo to face Josh Allen and the 9-1 Bills. The Bills have never hosted a game on Thanksgiving, and for their first one, they get the biggest game of the NFL regular season.

Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, with the AFC’s No. 1 seed in play. (Getty Images)

Sure, Chiefs-Bills doesn’t have the history of Steelers-Browns, Cowboys-Eagles or Packers-Lions. But try telling someone in Buffalo that Kansas City isn’t a rival. Mahomes and Allen met in the playoffs four times in five seasons, twice with a trip to the Super Bowl on the line. The Chiefs ended the Bills’ season all four times. And I’m guessing nobody in Buffalo needs me to explain what "13 seconds" means.

DK METCALF DISQUALIFIED FROM STEELERS GAME FOR UNSPORTSMANLIKE PENALTIES INCLUDING POKING OPPONENT'S FACEMASK

Kansas City certainly looked ready Sunday. Travis Kelce had a vintage Kelce game, catching six passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns, both before halftime. Mahomes threw for 324 yards and three scores, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson added 105 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That’s three straight games with at least 34 points for the Chiefs.

Buffalo, meanwhile, won by 17 on a day when Allen threw two interceptions and didn’t run the ball once. How often do you get to say that about a Bills win? Allen still threw for 304 yards, and Miami managed three field goals. I wouldn’t count on Mahomes being quite that accommodating.

The Bills have won five straight regular-season games against the Chiefs. A sixth would put Buffalo at 10-1, two games ahead of Kansas City. If the Chiefs win, they’ll close out Thanksgiving night tied with Buffalo at 9-2 and holding the head-to-head tiebreaker. That’s a pretty big swing for a Bills team trying to earn the AFC’s No. 1 seed for the first time in the Josh Allen era.

Joe Brady, pictured with quarterback Josh Allen during the national anthem, will face the Kansas City Chiefs for the first time as Buffalo’s head coach on Thanksgiving night. (Getty Images)

Allen has won all three of his regular-season trips to Arrowhead and lost all three of his playoff games there. Mahomes has won in Buffalo in January, too, beating the Bills 27-24 in the divisional round after the 2023 season. But both times these two played for the AFC championship, Buffalo had to go to Kansas City. A win Thursday gives Allen a much better shot at making Mahomes get on a plane in late January.

And if you’re wondering what happened the last time Buffalo did earn the No. 1 seed, the 1993 Bills won the AFC championship game at home, 30-13. The team they beat to get to the Super Bowl? The Kansas City Chiefs.

BUFFALO BILLS TAP HOMETOWN HEROES GOO GOO DOLLS FOR THANKSGIVING NIGHT HALFTIME CONCERT

Of course, the Bengals would prefer to host the AFC championship game themselves. They’re 7-2 heading into Monday Night Football against Washington, and I suspect they’ll be rooting for Kansas City on Thanksgiving. A Chiefs win would give Buffalo its second loss, and the Bengals don’t get a shot at the Bills in the regular season. They do, however, get the Chiefs at home on Dec. 13.

And yes, the Broncos and Jaguars are in the mix for the No. 1 seed, too. Jacksonville even went into Cincinnati and beat the Bengals. But when I ranked my Super Bowl contenders at the halfway point, I had three AFC teams in the top tier. If it’s my money, I’m still betting the AFC runs through Kansas City, Buffalo or Cincinnati.

So if the Chiefs win on Thanksgiving and the Bengals keep winning, Chiefs-Bengals on Dec. 13 might be the biggest game of the NFL regular season. That gives me about two weeks to ask my editor if changing "Bills" to "Bengals" and running this article again counts as plagiarizing myself.

Week 11 didn’t look particularly good on paper, and most of Sunday’s early games looked about the same on TV. If the NFL wants to wash the taste of those lopsided matchups out of our mouths, though, Week 12 ought to do it.

Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs can pull even with the Bills at 9-2 and claim the head-to-head tiebreaker with a win in Buffalo on Thanksgiving night. (Getty Images)

The Packers visit the Rams on Wednesday night. The Bears and Lions open Thanksgiving with a game that could help decide the NFC North, and we get Seahawks-49ers on Sunday afternoon. I’d happily watch any of those three, and none is the game I’m looking forward to most. That would be Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving night.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The only downside is that three of those four games will be over before we even get to Friday. Then again, am I really going to complain about only having to wait four days to see Mahomes and Allen play each other?

Ask me again Sunday at 1 p.m. when I’m trying to decide which game gets the main TV in my living room and Saints-Bengals is probably my best option.

articles.title: Travis Kelce passes Rob Gronkowski on all-time NFL list with two-touchdown game for Chiefs
articles.excerpt:
Rob Gronkowski and Julian Edelman reacted to the nail-biting win that the Kansas City Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes pulled off over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Travis Kelce had himself a day against the Ariz...
articles.body_text:
Rob Gronkowski and Julian Edelman reacted to the nail-biting win that the Kansas City Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes pulled off over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Travis Kelce had himself a day against the Arizona Cardinals, and with two more touchdowns on his Pro Football Hall of Fame resume, he made some NFL history.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end’s eight-yard touchdown snag to get his team in the end zone first on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium marked the 109th of his career.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Kelce moved past the great Rob Gronkowski for third on the NFL’s all-time tight end touchdowns list. They had been tied at 108 scores, which the New England Patriots star finished his career with.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce stands on the field after defeating the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 22, 2026, at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Only Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115), both Hall of Fame tight ends, are above Kelce on the list. He certainly has a chance to live atop the list entirely one day if he continues to get opportunities like he did on Sunday.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes found Kelce later in this 34-7 blowout at home for an even more impressive 22-yard touchdown grab, where the veteran pass-catcher fought off two tacklers before falling into the end zone.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Kelce, with his superstar wife Taylor Swift in her usual suite looking down on the field, hauled in six of his seven targets for 74 yards with his two scores.

Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce celebrates after a touchdown during the first quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo., on Nov. 22, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Mahomes himself had a tremendous day when he dropped back, going 27-of-39 for 324 yards with three touchdowns. With the game very out of reach in the fourth quarter, key starters like Mahomes and Kelce were getting some rest on the sideline.

This Sunday also marked Kelce’s 100th regular season game at the beloved Arrowhead Stadium, making him only the fourth player in team history to do so. He’s spent his entire career in Kansas City, which took him in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft out of Cincinnati.

It’s unknown what the future holds for Kelce after this season, as retirement has been a topic of conversation in back-to-back offseasons. The question will likely pop up again after the 2026 campaign, though Kelce hasn’t given an indication of what he wishes to do just yet.

Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce scores a touchdown during the second quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo., on Nov. 22, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Until then, he’ll continue to impact the Chiefs, who are now 8-2 on the season, as they aim for another Super Bowl victory.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack
articles.excerpt:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours o...
articles.body_text:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.

The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.

Initial reports said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press.

Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine, marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war.

Though Ukraine began the war with no navy, it has developed a sea drone capability that threatened Russian warships in the Black Sea. The Russian fleet has been forced to retreat to the eastern port of Novorossiysk because Sevastopol in occupied Crimea had become unsafe.

Hours later, a Russia-linked cargo ship said to be carrying military supplies, the Ascalon, was hit by a sea drone off the coast of Benghazi. Video showed the drone heading directly towards one end of the vessel, again causing a major explosion.

Libyan naval forces ‌rescued the vessel’s crew, the ‌sources added. The health ministry said some crew members were in stable condition with minor injuries. The number of injured and their nationalities are not known.

Benghazi is controlled by the self-styled Libyan National Army, led by Gen Khalifa Haftar, which controls eastern and southern Libya and has been aligned with Russia.

There was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities, and no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range attacks against Russia far beyond the frontlines.

The ‌eastern-based Libyan authority said port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that ​normal operations would resume once the fire was brought under control and the site secured.

It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and ⁠a threat to maritime safety, saying it would take ​legal and ​diplomatic measures against ​anyone found responsible.

“The Libyan government will not ​allow Libyan ‌ports, territory or territorial ​waters ​to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.

The specialist website Naval News earlier identified the ship attacked as the Merkury, a Russian corvette – the smallest class of warship, smaller than a frigate – and said it had almost been certainly destroyed.

HI Sutton, a naval analyst, said the attack was probably conducted by sea drones, after a photograph of one emerged apparently taken off the Libyan coast. The drone, he said, “is also likely the type used in the subsequent attack”. Similar-looking drones were involved in the subsequent attack on the Ascalon cargo ship.

If it is confirmed that Ukraine has been able to blow up or seriously damage a Russian warship in Benghazi, it would represent one of its most successful naval strikes during the almost five-year war.

But it also represents a risky extension of the fighting far beyond eastern Europe, in an incident that could affect civilians on another continent and the working of the port.

A small unit of Ukrainian special forces operatives has been based at Misrata, western Libya, and is believed to have coordinated drone attacks on Russian tankers and transport ships in the past year.

Russian ships regularly make use of the port, which has a growing military importance to the Kremlin, to supply Russian mercenary forces in Africa and as a base in the Mediterranean since the country lost its bases in Syria.

Separately, a fire onboard a Russian cargo ship that was ⁠struck by drones in the ⁠Baltic Sea continued to smoulder ​on Sunday, Finland’s border guard said, with emergency services from Finland, Russia and Estonia working together to put out the blaze.

The Finnish military said the strike on the Sparta II ⁠on Saturday was probably carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters, where it remained at anchor. The 16 crew members were evacuated on to a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly ⁠injured.

On Sunday, visible flames had been put out, with operations focusing on cooling down the containers and stabilising the vessel, Finnish authorities said.

The ship, bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, had been damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland Island, Finland’s defence forces said, corroborating an account by Russian officials. Kyiv has sent waves of military drones towards the Leningrad region on Russia’s north-west coast this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling on to Nato territory.

The risk of ⁠further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, could not be ruled ​out, Ivo Värk, the Estonian navy commander, told the public ​broadcaster ERR on Sunday.

Finland’s military said last ​week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.

articles.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
articles.excerpt:
Russian ship engulfed in flames after explosion at Libyan port

An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has...
articles.body_text:
Russian ship engulfed in flames after explosion at Libyan port

An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.

The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government.

The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.

Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said.

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.

Satellite imagery showed a ship on fire at the port

US-based intelligence firm Vantor collected high-resolution images that it said showed Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette (Merkury) - a Russian navy ship - moored in the port on Saturday, and on Sunday showed most of the same ship capsized and sunk with only the forward bow still visible.

The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship - which it did not name or identify - was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.

Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.

GNS condemned the attack on a ship inside a Libyan port, and called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty. It said Libya was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.

Separately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli - the Government of National Unity (GNU) - warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.

GNU said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".

Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.

Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.

Although it has not been officially confirmed who was behind the attack, there is little doubt, according to Jalel Harchaoui, Libya specialist at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).

"Ukraine is the only actor brazen enough to pull something like that off," he told the BBC. "If I were to bet my own money, I would bet that it was the Ukrainians."

If confirmed, it would not be the first time Ukrainian forces had carried out an operation of this sort. In March, Russia accused Ukraine of targeting the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta with "uncrewed sea drones" launched from the Libyan coast.

As well as having an economic impact on Russia, hampering the ability of their so-called shadow fleet of tankers to export oil and gas, attacks like this are seen as humiliating to the Kremlin, according to Harchaoui.

But it is not only Moscow that will want to react to this latest incident. The ship was in the region as part of a deal with the government of eastern Libya - allied with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the Libyan National Army.

Harchaoui said Haftar will take the attack as a personal slight. "You're going to have a response by the Haftar family. They will ask questions about who is hosting the Ukrainians."

articles.title: Trump warns of new strikes against Iran after new year, calls negotiators ‘professional tap dancers’
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Chief Congressional correspondent Trey Yingst joins 'Fox News Live' to weigh in on President Trump's remarks after new Iran aerial attacks targeted U.S. military facilities.

President Donald...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Chief Congressional correspondent Trey Yingst joins 'Fox News Live' to weigh in on President Trump's remarks after new Iran aerial attacks targeted U.S. military facilities.

President Donald Trump is warning that he is inclined to order military strikes against Iran after the new year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement, dismissing ongoing diplomatic talks with Tehran as meaningless.

In exclusive comments Sunday to Fox News, the president accused Iranian negotiators of stalling while continuing to escalate hostilities following the U.S. elections.

TRUMP KEEPS SIGNALING AN END TO IRAN WAR, BUT EXPERT WARNS A CRUCIAL PIECE OF HIS STRATEGY IS MISSING

If negotiations with Iran collapse, the U.S. is likely to move quickly to degrade Tehran’s military capabilities — a campaign analysts say would begin with missile systems, naval assets and command networks before escalating to more controversial targets. (Yuri Gripas/Abaca/Bloomberg via Getty Images:  Sasan / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images)

"They’re more aggressive now than before the election," Trump said, characterizing Iranian officials as "professional tap dancers."

"They talk all the time, all they do is talk, but it’s all b------," he added.

The remarks come as the U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports amid broader conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, and as Trump predicted that tit-for-tat strikes will continue between American and Iranian forces.

PROTESTERS CALL FOR REGIME CHANGE IN IRAN FOLLOWING DEADLY CRASH THAT KILLED 13 OIL AND GAS WORKERS

Trump also dared Tehran to challenge the U.S. naval siege.
