articles.title: South Korea education minister resigns after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
articles.excerpt:
Choi Kyo-jin said he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams, which this year had phones banned and checks for cameras hidden in clothing

South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday...
articles.body_text:
Choi Kyo-jin said he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams, which this year had phones banned and checks for cameras hidden in clothing

South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted in the lead-up to the country’s key university entrance exams.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial university entrance exam known as the suneung.

The confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures for the entrance exams last week, including blocking public wifi in testing areas.

But the education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, struggled to reassure the public, and teachers’ unions criticised the government response as belated.

The annual eight-hour suneung determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

“The exam concluded without any major incidents … However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance,” Choi wrote on X.

“Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation,” he added.

President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old Choi replied: “Due to my age, I am not confident I could.” His response quickly drew public backlash.

Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday’s exam, where a vice minister instead announced the preventive measures.

South Korea goes to great lengths to ensure the smooth running of the suneung. Aircraft take-offs and landings are rescheduled during the 25-minute English listening paper to minimise noise, while artillery fire and tank movements are suspended. The stock market opens an hour late and cars are stopped 200 metres from every centre.

In the aftermath of the cheating scandal earlier this month, the government announced that smart devices would have to be turned off and handed in for the suneung, while bags left in corridors would be checked for any devices that were still on. Exam officials would also inspect all candidates’ glasses and watches, as well as their collars, sleeves and buttons for concealed cameras.

The government also sent emergency alerts to every phone in the country, which sounded at full volume and could not be silenced, in the hope of catching out anyone who has not handed in their device.

Officials said 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during Thursday’s exam, nearly half of which were detected through the emergency alerts.

articles.title: Fossil fuel impasse pushes COP31 climate talks into second day of overtime
articles.excerpt:
Turkish officials have asked negotiators at the COP31 climate summit to consider a last-minute proposal as talks stretched into a second day of overtime over the fossil fuels issue.

“We believe that ...
articles.body_text:
Turkish officials have asked negotiators at the COP31 climate summit to consider a last-minute proposal as talks stretched into a second day of overtime over the fossil fuels issue.

“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary session on Saturday.

Kurum, who is also Turkiye’s environment minister, said the conference would reconvene later on Sunday morning to approve the deal.

The latest text was not immediately made public, and it was unclear if negotiators had received the wording overnight, which would give nations only a few hours to submit objections and changes.

An earlier draft had drawn strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels, the largest contributors to climate change.

Kurum said he ⁠believed concerns around fossil fuels had ‌been addressed, as had those ‌around helping developing countries finance their adaptations to climate change.

The new ‌text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is ‌leading the talks; Turkiye, which is hosting the meeting; and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.

Delegations had until 03:00 GMT on Sunday to ‌raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 06:00 GMT to ⁠begin approving ⁠it.

The summit’s agreement is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which drives heatwaves, floods and other disasters.

An opening draft from Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.

Key issues that slowed down the agreement included how much effort countries should make to wean themselves off fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and gas.

Other issues included whether to encourage industrial carbon capture and storage of pollutants, as well as whether ramping up electricity should only be done with renewables, such as wind and solar, or also involve other sources like natural gas and coal.

To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions.

The two-week talks in the Turkish city of Antalya were due to end on Friday.

In a letter sent on Saturday to this year’s cohosts, Turkiye and Australia, 100 civil society groups warned that they were “on course to preside over one of the most disappointing COPs” the UN has ever held.

The letter stated there were only hours left “to save this COP from becoming a low point of three decades of climate negotiations”.

In the lead-up to these talks, the United Nations said the world would likely blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

articles.title: Georgia has top College Football Playoff seed in sight with dominating road win over No 21 South Carolina
articles.excerpt:
Fans and coaches across college football are erupting over a Top 25 stacked with 6-4 SEC teams and two-loss Alabama getting propped up while Indiana gets penalized.

Georgia showed exactly why it is t...
articles.body_text:
Fans and coaches across college football are erupting over a Top 25 stacked with 6-4 SEC teams and two-loss Alabama getting propped up while Indiana gets penalized.

Georgia showed exactly why it is the top-ranked team in college football on Saturday.

The Bulldogs beat No. 21 South Carolina 34-6 at Williams-Brice Stadium, as the Georgia defense suffocated the Gamecocks' offense. With the win, Georgia now has the top spot in the College Football Playoff firmly in their grasp.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

South Carolina had just 218 yards of offense on the day. South Carolina star quarterback LaNorris Sellers was held in check, as he completed just 10 of 18 passes for 87 yards and a touchdown.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Running back Nate Frazier #3 of the Georgia Bulldogs rushes the ball during a college football game against the South Carolina Gamecocks on Nov. 21, 2026, at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

While South Carolina's offense never quite got out of the gate, it took Georgia a little bit of time to get things rolling.

The Gamecocks opened the game with a field goal, and the Bulldogs responded with a first-quarter field goal of their own, tying the game 3-3. South Carolina also converted a field goal on their second drive, going up 6-3.

The Bulldogs' offense didn't find the end zone until later in the second quarter, when it capped off a 10-play, 88-yard drive with a Nate Frazier touchdown, giving Georgia a 10-6 lead going into halftime.

Georgia got the ball to begin the third quarter, and they broke through with an explosive play. On third-and-2, quarterback Gunner Stockton found tight end Jaden Reddell for a 66-yard completion that brought Georgia to South Carolina's 1-yard line.

Georgia head coach Kirby Smart looks on in the first half against South Carolina during a game at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C., on Nov. 21, 2026. (Getty Images)

A couple of plays later, Frazier punched the ball into the end zone for his second touchdown of the game, putting Georgia up 17-6. Later in the third quarter, the Bulldogs tacked on another field goal to go up 20-6.

The Bulldogs effectively put the game away when they marched down the field with an 11-play, 91-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. Wide receiver Craig Dandridge scored a 14-yard touchdown on a play fake that had South Carolina's defense fooled, putting Georgia up 27-6.

Georgia tacked on another touchdown at the end of the fourth quarter to go up 34-6, as they scored 31 unanswered points after falling behind 6-3.

Frazier had 23 carries for 94 yards and two touchdowns on the day for Georgia.

Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton scrambles out of the pocket during the first half of an NCAA college football game against South Carolina on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Columbia, S.C. (AP Photo/Artie Walker Jr.)

Georgia plays rival Georgia Tech in their next game on Saturday, and a win would all but guarantee the top seed in the College Football Playoff.

articles.excerpt:

articles.body_text:
A shooting Saturday at an entertainment venue left three people dead in Parma, Ohio. (Google Maps)

Three people were killed and another was injured during a shooting at a baby shower at an Ohio event venue Saturday evening, according to local reports.

The shooting occurred around 6 p.m. inside Pandora's Magical Events Venue, located at 5331 Ridge Road in Parma, Ohio, according to a statement released by the Parma Police Department.

Responding officers determined that four people had been shot during an "exchange of gunfire."

A 17-year-old girl, a 19-year-old man and a 45-year-old man were found dead at the scene, according to police.

PREGNANT MOM JUST 4 DAYS FROM GIVING BIRTH AMONG 8 KILLED IN PENNSYLVANIA MASSACRE: REPORTS

Parma police Public Information Officer Scott Traxler told FOX 8/WJW that the 19-year-old victim was the unborn child's father and the 45-year-old victim was the pregnant woman's father. Police identified the 19-year-old man as one of those involved in the exchange of gunfire.

A fourth victim, a 39-year-old woman, suffered a gunshot wound to the leg that was considered non-life-threatening, police said.

Police also said a 29-year-old man allegedly involved in the exchange of gunfire was taken into custody following the shooting. Authorities have not publicly identified the man in custody or announced a possible motive.

Traxler told Fox News Digital that authorities were continuing to verify additional details surrounding the shooting.

Multiple firearms were recovered from the scene, according to police.

In a social media post, the Parma Police Department said officers were investigating a shooting involving multiple victims in the 5300 block of Ridge Road.

"Parma Police Department extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in this tragic incident," the department wrote.

"There is no danger to the public," police added.

Police said the families of those killed have been notified.

The Parma Police Department's Detective Bureau is investigating the shooting.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

Michael Sinkewicz is a writer for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to michael.sinkewicz@fox.com

articles.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
articles.excerpt:
Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected

Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.

At 38, he is among the young people seeking elec...
articles.body_text:
Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected

Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.

At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.

He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.

"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.

But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.

Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.

The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.

His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.

Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).

Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.

The contrast is striking in a country with one of the world's youngest populations, where young people have repeatedly demonstrated their ability to shape political debate and mobilise for change.

In the previous election, Obi, then 61, galvanised millions of young Nigerians through a social media-driven movement known as the "Obedients".

His campaign promised a break from the established political order, appealing particularly to young people struggling to find jobs and earn a decent living.

But his failure to win the presidency left many of his supporters disillusioned.

"At the time we were so hopeful, but unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted, which made many lose hope in the system," former Obedient Nonso Chukwudi tells the BBC.

The movement had built on the momentum of the EndSars protests in 2020, which grew into one of Nigeria's biggest youth-led movement in decades.

Initially sparked by anger over police brutality, the demonstrators developed into a wider call for political reform, accountability and greater youth participation in governance.

But the protests were eventually crushed by the authorities. About 56 were reportedly killed, although officials dispute this figure, while hundreds were arrested and some had their bank accounts frozen.

Both EndSars and the Obedients demonstrated the capacity of young Nigerians to mobile around political causes.

Abdulhadi Dalhatu hopes to be president one day but bemoans the financial obstacles needed to contest

But turning that enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has proved much harder.

Hajara Musa, 33, is among those who have lost faith in the political system. She has no plans to register or vote in the near future.

"I just feel like things are already determined and I'll just be wasting my time. It is going to be the same people all over again," she tells the BBC.

The electoral register appears to reflect this growing disillusionment.

Although the number of registered voters has increased by 10 million to over 103 million since the last election, enrolment of those under 35 has actually fallen, by about seven million.

Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023.

Nigeria's electoral commission, Inec, says it has made efforts to encourage more young people to register ahead of the 2027 general elections.

This includes appointing nine ambassadors from the entertainment industry, spanning film, music and comedy, to reach younger audiences.

But the figures suggest these efforts have yet to make a significant difference.

Dalhatu says he understands the frustration but argues that young Nigerians cannot expect change, if they stay away from the political process.

"Unfortunately, many prefer to just post on social media" instead of getting involved, he says.

Of course being young does not mean you are necessarily the best candidate.

For those who want to participate, there is a formidable obstacle to getting into politics - money.

Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023

Dalhatu dreams of becoming president one day, but says he has previously had to abandon campaigns because he could not raise enough funds.

The cost of running for office in Nigeria is notoriously high.

Under the Electoral Act, presidential candidates were allowed to spend up to 5bn naira (£2.8m; $3.7m) on campaigns ahead of the 2023 elections. That spending limit has since been doubled.

The cost of nomination forms alone puts the presidency beyond the reach of most aspiring young Nigerians.

The ruling All Progressive Congress (APC), along with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have each set their presidential nomination fee at 100m naira ($74,000; £56,000), making it extremely hard for new challengers to emerge.

Since the return to democracy in 1999, only two parties have governed Nigeria - the PDP from 1999 to 2015 and the APC since 2015.

These parties, alongside the ADC, formed last year by politicians who had defected from the other two, have established nationwide network of branches, supporters and campaigners.

Those aspiring candidates without the financial resources to secure nomination forms and compete in the internal party contests of the main parties have little chances of becoming president.

The barriers are also evident in the National Assembly.

Not one of Nigeria's 109 senators is under 40, while only 14 of the 360 members of the House of Representatives fall into that age group.

"I have been in politics for many years and I will tell you that young people in this country lack the resources to become president," says Dalhatu, who is running under Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.

Atiku Abubakar is seeking the presidency for a seventh time

Fatima Zahra Umar, a young politician in the APC who has previously tried to run for a seat in the House of Representatives, agrees.

"Young Nigerians are poor. Nigerian politics is cash-intensive, so participation is guided by money," she says, adding that young people are often content with having a bit of influence as a special advisor to a senior politician.

But political analyst Seun Ajayi believes the problems go beyond the financial barriers.

"We have some of the most brilliant young persons in the world, but they are either not interested in politics or feel satisfied when given a small role in government," he says.

"The old men are not going to sit idle and allow us to push them out. We have to fight for the big positions, but at the moment I don't see the zeal."

Umar believes changing attitudes towards young leadership is equally important.

"Culturally, we are not primed to trust or accept the brilliance of a younger person, so it will be very difficult," she says.

"Old men are still holding on to the system."

Some Nigerians took inspiration from the wave of success of young candidates in the recent midterm elections in the US, some of whom have roots in Africa.

"America Has Done It, Can Nigerians Do the Same?" entertainer Charly Boy wrote on X, in a post that was widely shared.

He said the US results served as a warning to Nigerian politicians that no matter how powerful the political machine, voters can change the direction of government.

He called on young people to interrogate candidates about their past promises: "Has life improved? Where are the jobs, security and affordable living?

"Democracy is not a spectator sport, nor is it about sharing rice," he wrote.

articles.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
articles.excerpt:
Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament

Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Col...
articles.body_text:
Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament

Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.

She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.

He told her he liked her name, and she confessed that it was an alias. She was a runaway, she said - and was being held against her will, hundreds of miles from home, though she didn't know exactly where. The girl, 17, and had been missing for more than a year.

Stunned, Landon felt "helpless," he says - and, after learning more details over two weeks of chatting, he decided to tell his mother, Khristina on 31 October this year. The 41-year-old nurse and mother of five was putting Halloween makeup on her younger children for trick-or-treating when he briefed her.

That set the mother and son on a path to track down his friend, contact her mother, cooperate with the FBI - and ultimately witness the rescue of the teen - only 24 hours after Landon first alerted Khristina to her plight.

"She had one opportunity to reach out her hand and ask for help, and she chose me," Khristina says of the girl, who was 15 when she went missing.

A screenshot shows Khristina on a call with the girl as she showed her the knife her alleged captor kept under his pillow

The Tresps have shared with BBC screenshots of communication with the girl and a photo matching the criminal complaint to corroborate their story.

Landon first told his mother about "Jenny" - whose identity the BBC is protecting - in mid-October, a few weeks before the rescue.

"He had mentioned something about maybe a week or so into talking to her that he met a girl online, and she was really sweet," says Khristina - who cautioned him that "you don't always know who's on the other side of the screen".

"She's just having a really hard time and looking for a friend," he told her.

But Landon was becoming increasingly concerned as Jenny told him more about her situation.

They'd met playing Among Us, a game Landon describes as "kind of like online space Clue".

After telling Landon that she was a runaway, "Jenny" said an older man had taken her across state lines and wouldn't let her leave. She was the subject of a missing person investigation, and she sent Landon links to stories about her disappearance. But she believed police were no longer looking for her.

Jenny was scared and desperate, and that's why Landon went to his mother.

Her maternal instincts on high alert, Khristina contacted Jenny herself on Discord, the encrypted platform.

During the conversation, Khristina said she told the Colorado mother how she'd been through "years of abuse in her life and lots and lots of problems".

Within hours, Jenny started calling Khristina "mama".

Among Us supports cross platform play online with 4-15 players on various devices

The Colorado mother knew things were serious when she read the missing persons articles. Jenny knew she was in Oregon and gave the name of a city, but she didn't know where she was being held exactly. Khristina knew she needed more. She told Jenny to find a piece of mail or another document in the house that had a full name on it, which the girl did.

"That's when I went to work," Khristina says, delving into tax and property records.

Khristina narrowed down addresses, then searched them on a real estate site to find pictures. She showed the photos to Jenny, who confirmed that the second one was where she was being held.

The "next thing she asked me was to please not tell anyone until [her captor] was gone - that he did have weapons in the house and she was very scared," Khristina said.

Jenny promised Khristina she'd call her back through the game platform when he left the next morning, and in the meantime Khristina began looking for the law enforcement agency that had been assigned to the missing teen's case. She contacted Jenny's mother on social media, spoke briefly to her on the phone and then got a call from an FBI agent.

"Have you seen her alive?'" the agent asked Khristina.

"And I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her, and she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'," Khristina recalled.

When Jenny called Khristina back after her alleged captor left home, the FBI monitored their conversation. According to the criminal complaint's record of the conversation, Jenny explained how she'd met Adam Hunter Harmel on social media in May 2025.

He'd told her he was disabled and his hips were "messed up," offering Jenny money if she'd help get him to Oregon.

After he picked her up in Utah, however, Harmel threw her phone into a river, drove her to Oregon and kept her in the basement. He forced her to sleep against the wall in his bed, with a knife under his pillow, to prevent her from escaping. He gave Jenny a cell phone with no ability to make calls, but it could connect to wifi, which is how she played the online game.

The 39-year-old "would become violent and aggressive", the document says, which included hitting her and sexually assaulting her.

He also allegedly forced Jenny to remove her braces with pliers so she wouldn't be identifiable.

As Khristina and the FBI heard all of this, law enforcement were staging to bring Jenny to safety, after being alerted to her whereabouts.

While Harmel was out of the home, officers were sent to the street and the address, and Khristina was prepping Jenny for her run to freedom.

She'd unsuccessfully tried escaping before, she told Khristina.

Law enforcement was "phenomenal…giving me an update, you know, 'We're nine minutes out, we're seven minutes out,'" says Khristina, who was on the phone with Jenny the entire time, her son Landon watching at her side.

Khristina could hear other people in the home with Jenny, and she was afraid that someone would catch wind of what was happening and harm the girl.

But she kept any of those fears from Jenny.

"I want you to take three deep breaths with me," she told the teen. "When an officer tells me to go, and I relay that message to you, I want you to run up those stairs as fast as you can … Grab that basement door.

"I want you to keep going down that hallway and grab that front door… do not stop.'"

The mother and son watched breathlessly as Jenny ran into the arms of a state trooper.

Harmel is now in federal custody and has been charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Local Oregon media also reported he'd been accused of sexually abusing a six-year-old in the months before Jenny disappeared - and a sexual abuse protective order was granted against him in March 2025.

A lawyer for the defendant did not respond to a BBC request for comment.

Jenny, meanwhile, remains in daily communication with Khristina and Landon - who still enjoys playing online games with her.

"Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina says. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away."

"She's doing great for what she's gone through."

They haven't met in person yet, but they're in the process of trying to make that happen.

"I hope I can put my arms around her soon," Khristina says.

articles.title: Ranking the top six 'Grand Theft Auto VI' in-game radio stations, from V-Rock to Vice City FM
articles.excerpt:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the ‘Gutfeld!’ panel discuss the phenomenon of Grand Theft Auto 6.

If you’ve played even five minutes of "Grand Theft Auto VI" since its release, you know just how imme...
articles.body_text:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the ‘Gutfeld!’ panel discuss the phenomenon of Grand Theft Auto 6.

If you’ve played even five minutes of "Grand Theft Auto VI" since its release, you know just how immersive this video game is.

There are miles of swamps and beaches to explore, realistic NPC interactions and I even made an entire article about how realistic the game’s version of South Florida is when compared to its real-life counterpart.

But one mechanic that has been included in the new game that’s been around since the early days of the series are the radio stations, and "GTA VI" has the most diverse radio dial yet.

REDDIT'S BIRDING COMMUNITY GOES WILD AS UNIQUE 'GRAND THEFT AUTO 6' FEATURE COMES TO LIGHT

Ads for "Grand Theft Auto VI" are seen in New York City ahead of the game's release. (Photo by Richard B. Levine)

All in all, there are 22 unique radio stations in the game, and each of them offers a different soundtrack to your wheeling and stealing as you traverse through Leonida.

Being a huge fan of the series and music in general, I thought it would be fun to rank my six favorite "GTA VI" radio stations.

This wasn’t easy, as there are a ton of great stations to choose from, and I even had to omit a few that I really liked (sorry, Back Country Radio).

With that said, let’s rank the best that "GTA VI" has to offer in the form of music.

By virtue of hitting the "quantity over quality" metrics, Flash FM sneaks its way onto the list at number six.

Don't get me wrong, there are heaps of awful songs on this station, but there are some gems in there too.

Promotional displays and storefronts in The Hague, Netherlands, showcase anticipation for Grand Theft Auto VI on Nov. 18, 2026, as the highly anticipated open-world blockbuster takes over retail stores ahead of its global midnight release. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

Echosmith, Foster The People, Gwen Stefani, and MGMT will have Millennials bobbing their heads as they commit vehicular homicide (in the game), and newcomers like Ella Langley and Addison Rae offer enough to be passable cruising songs when there's nothing else on.

Flash FM isn't the stalwart it was back in the '80s for "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City," but there is enough fun to be had here for this station to find its way into the rotation.

This one might be a bit of a nostalgia pick for me, but I don't care.

Having grown up and gone to high school in South Florida, a lot of the songs on this station were popular right around the time my life was centered around algebra tests and getting rejected by chicks, so playing a game where I can drive around a virtual representation of my hometown while blaring rap songs that were popular 15 years ago is an auto win.

If you're into 2000s and 2010s rap, you'll probably have your radio dial locked on Dirty South Classics, with heavy hitters like Lil Wayne, Outkast, Drake, Rick Ross and even Jay Z being well represented here.

There is no better feeling than cruising Miami Beach at night listening to "No Lie" by 2Chainz, and it's even cooler when that is also a core memory from your adolescence, minus the cocaine and dead hookers.

Now we are getting into rarified air, and Vice City FM begins a string of stations with way more good than bad on them.

For those of you who wanted the '80s vibes of "Vice City" to carry over to the new game, you're in luck.

MIAMI HEAT UNVEIL VICE CITY COURT FOR 'GRAND THEFT AUTO VI'-THEMED CLASH WITH MILWAUKEE BUCKS

A poster for the Grand Theft Auto VI video game, which will be released on Nov. 19, 2026, is displayed at a GameStop store on Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, in Colma, Calif. (AP Photo/Jeff Chiu)

Vice City FM is a carryover from the old Playstation 2 game, and the songs you'll find on here will have you thinking you hopped in a DeLorean and landed in 1986.

Genesis, Culture Club, Lionel Richie, Billy Idol, The Cars and so much more, you'll be pulling out the AquaNet and legwarmers before your first hour of gameplay.

The neon lights of South Florida mesh perfectly with the 80s vibes, and this station makes for a cool nighttime drive soundtrack.

For an added bonus, Weird Al Yankovic is one of the in-game DJs, which I thought was a nice touch.

Metal, metal and more metal. That's what you're going to find on The Chamber.

While I'm partial to the older stuff, this station has a great mix of classic and newer metal to bridge the generational gap for headbangers.

If you're a spiritual Boomer like me, you'll be happy to know acts like Iron Maiden, Judas Priest, Megadeth and, of course, Metallica are littered all over The Chamber.

New-school metal disciples will be pleased to hear the likes of Linkin Park, System of a Down, Tool and Sepultura mixed in.

Committing virtual crimes is so much more fun when it's set to the brutal riffing and blistering solos of Judas Priest's "Freewheel Burning," but don't just take my word for it, try it yourself.

And hey, the station is hosted by Slayer's Tom Araya and Kerry King, so you know it's curated by two legends.

Can you name a better combination than the sun-soaked streets of South Florida and some soothing yacht rock?

Of course you can't, which is why Emotion 98.3 is sitting in the silver medal spot for "GTA VI" radio stations.

Emotion makes its triumphant return as one of the stations featured in "GTA: Vice City," and its setlist will have you looking for the nearest super yacht to steal so that you can enjoy the songs properly.

You want soft rock? How does Ace, Chicago, The Doobie Brothers, and Bruce Hornsby sound?

An ad for "Grand Theft Auto VI" appears on the side of a building in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello)

I spent my entire life being serenaded by these guys while navigating the intracoastal waterways of South Florida, and now I get to do it in a video game.

If you played "GTA: Vice City," you know how legendary this station was.

Well, it's back and better than ever, featuring a wide range of classic rock artists that offer the best company on any long drive around Leonida.

There are too many bangers to even count, but I'll try: Def Leppard, AC/DC, Aerosmith, Dire Straits, Foreigner, Blue Oyster Cult, Motley Crue, Styx, and ZZ Top, just to name a few.

Seriously, I haven't even mentioned another half dozen artists who rank as some of my favorites of all time.

Oh, and they have Van Halen, too. In case I needed to nerd out any more than I already am.

I also love how they included several Tom Petty songs, given his connection to the Sunshine State.

Finally, the station is hosted by Lindsey Buckingham of Fleetwood Mac fame and Michael Freaking McDonald.

When the king of Blue Eyed Soul is spinning tunes, it's probably a station worth listening to.

articles.title: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
articles.excerpt:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south.

In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd indepe...
articles.body_text:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south.

In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun said Lebanon faces two interconnected fateful tests: the “Israeli occupation of parts of our land” and “foreign interference” from “some influential parties in the Iranian regime” through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state.

These “two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked” mean that Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence, he added.

“Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives,” Aoun demanded of Israel.

Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres, including civilians as well as members of the Hezbollah armed group captured during fighting in southern Lebanon.

The president also pledged to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control, declaring that there would be “no weapons outside the state that take orders from, or serve the interests of foreign powers.”

“You must hand over your weapons,” Aoun said.

Lebanon’s government has promised to disarm Hezbollah, the Iran-backed Lebanese group whose arsenal has long outstripped that of the national army and that has justified its weapons as necessary to resist Israel.

Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement in June, following US-mediated talks, which included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanese territories and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.

But implementation has stalled, with Hezbollah refusing to surrender its weapons and Israel continuing to strike Lebanon.

On Saturday, Israeli strikes hit the districts of Nabatieh, Bint Jbeil and Marjayoun in southern Lebanon.

Al Jazeera correspondents reported that one of the air strikes hit the outskirts of Baraachit, a town in Bint Jbeil.

They said Baraachit came under Israeli gunfire at dawn and reported the movement of Israeli military vehicles on the outskirts of the town.

Israeli warplanes launched a second missile attack on the town of Kfar Tebnit in Nabatieh, after the first failed to detonate, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA).

The NNA reported that Israeli forces carried out three explosions in Wadi al-Khiam in the Marjayoun district, but gave no further details.

Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon have killed at least 4,386 people and wounded 12,407 others since March 2, when the latest Hezbollah-Israel war started.

Lebanon’s Ministry of Health said that since Israel began its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, Israeli strikes in Lebanon have killed 8,953 people and injured 30,643 others.

articles.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix betting guide: How to bet Saturday night's race on the strip
articles.excerpt:
Formula 1 legend Riccardo Patrese recounts the Caesars Palace Grand Prix and names some of his favorite tracks in the United States.

Vegas doesn't do anything quietly, and the Las Vegas Grand Prix is...
articles.body_text:
Formula 1 legend Riccardo Patrese recounts the Caesars Palace Grand Prix and names some of his favorite tracks in the United States.

Vegas doesn't do anything quietly, and the Las Vegas Grand Prix is no exception. The lights are on, the casinos are packed and Formula One cars will be screaming down the Strip at more than 200 miles per hour Saturday night. It's the one race on the calendar that feels like a show as much as a sporting event.

The betting board fits the setting. You can lay heavy juice on the favorite, or you can do what Vegas is built for and take a few swings. The race also has one more ingredient that makes it great to bet: chaos. Las Vegas averages 48.7 overtakes per race, more than Monza, Baku or Jeddah. The starting grid is a suggestion here, not a guarantee.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Here's how to bet the Las Vegas Grand Prix, from the race winner to a couple of fun swings further down the board.

WHAT IS A PARLAY BET? — HOW PARLAYS WORK, PAYOUTS AND RULES EXPLAINED

Antonelli was the fastest driver in qualifying, 0.258 seconds clear of Verstappen. A five-place penalty for an extra engine component dropped him to sixth. Oscar Piastri, Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll took 10-place penalties, and Piastri starts 17th after qualifying seventh.

This is the bet. The fastest car on the track is starting sixth, and you're getting almost 5-1 on it.

Antonelli has already won this year's drivers' championship, and he's chasing his 10th win of the season. He out-qualified everyone by a quarter of a second, and Mercedes brought a turbocharger upgrade this weekend that only he is running. Russell is on the older spec.

Starting from behind hasn't slowed him down this year. He won at Monza from 19th on the grid and finished fifth in Baku from 16th. Both are high-speed, low-downforce tracks, just like Vegas. Throw in a circuit that produces almost 50 overtakes per race, and five spots isn't much to make up.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli comes into the Miami Grand Prix as the championship leader. (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images)

Norris is the steady play. He starts third, he has four straight top-five finishes, and he took pole here last year before finishing second, a result later wiped out by a post-race disqualification.

He's also been quick all weekend. Norris set the fastest second sector in qualifying and finished just 0.093 seconds behind Verstappen's lap. In Brazil, he beat Verstappen to the line by 14.6 seconds. Starting on the second row of a track where passing is easy, a top-three finish is a reasonable ask.

NFL BETTING STRATEGY GUIDE: HOW TO BET ON FOOTBALL

Ferrari had a rough qualifying session, with both cars knocked out in Q2. After the penalties, Leclerc starts 10th. That's exactly why the price is +350, and exactly why I'm interested.

Leclerc has finished in the top four in all three of his Las Vegas starts. He's led 13 laps here, the third-most of anyone since the race began. He has six podiums this season, finished second at the U.S. Grand Prix and has finished in the top five in seven of his last eight races in North America.

Some drivers just have a feel for a track. Leclerc has one for this one. At 7-2, it's worth a bet.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli (centre) with Red Bull's Max Verstappen (left) and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc after Miami Grand Prix qualifying. (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images)

Here's a fun one. Piastri qualified seventh, then a 10-place engine penalty dropped him to 17th on the grid.

The pace is there. He was within about a second of pole in qualifying, and he's running the same McLaren that Norris has on the second row. A fast car starting 17th on the highest-overtaking track of the season is a natural fit for this market. If he finishes anywhere in the top 10, he'll likely be among the biggest movers on the night.

Verstappen has won here twice, in 2023 and 2025, and he starts on pole. I understand why he's the favorite.

But -130 means risking $130 to win $100 on a single race, at a track where the polesitter has less protection than almost anywhere else, with the fastest car in the field coming up behind him. Under the Vegas lights, I'd rather bet on chaos than lay juice on the chalk.

WHAT IS A MONEYLINE BET? — HOW MONEYLINE ODDS, PAYOUTS AND FAVORITES WORK

Red Bull driver Max Verstappen of the Netherlands steers his car during the Japanese Formula One Grand Prix at Suzuka in central Japan, Sunday, March 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Hiro Komae)

articles.title: Trump says Roger Clemens should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame 'immediately,' won't fully back Barry Bonds
articles.excerpt:
President Donald Trump discusses his posthumous pardon for baseball legend Pete Rose, analyzes Barry Bonds’ historic career and more on ‘Saturday in America.’

After giving a "complete and total pardo...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump discusses his posthumous pardon for baseball legend Pete Rose, analyzes Barry Bonds’ historic career and more on ‘Saturday in America.’

After giving a "complete and total pardon" to Pete Rose, President Donald Trump now has his eyes on getting another baseball legend into Cooperstown.

Trump said that seven-time Cy Young Award winner Roger Clemens should be in the Baseball Hall of Fame "immediately." Trump noted that Clemens has never been proven to have taken performance-enhancing drugs.

"Roger Clemens has never been proven to have taken drugs, and he swears that he didn't. And he went through committees and everything else, and they — he actually won a court case. And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs," Trump said during an appearance on Fox News' "Saturday in America."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Former New York Yankees pitcher Roger Clemens attends the Old Timer's Day Ceremony at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, N.Y., on Aug. 9, 2025. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Trump was referencing the court case in June 2012, in which Clemens was acquitted of all six counts of perjury, making false statements and obstructing Congress after a retrial over his denials of using steroids. Trump gushed over Clemens' illustrious resume.

Nicknamed "Rocket" for his overpowering fastball, Clemens won seven Cy Youngs, the most in the history of the sport. He won the 1986 AL MVP, was an 11-time All-Star and a two-time World Series champion, and won the ERA title seven times.

While Trump was steadfast in his belief that Clemens belongs in the Baseball Hall of Fame, he did not offer the same endorsement for Barry Bonds.

"Barry Bonds, I think (denied taking drugs) too. But a lot of, I mean, look, he was such a great player, you know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place," Trump said.

TRUMP SAYS HE'LL GIVE ROGER CLEMENS THE PRESIDENTIAL MEDAL OF FREEDOM: 'THIS SUPERSEDES ANYTHING I'VE DONE'

President Donald Trump shakes hands with former MLB player Roger Clemens after he was introduced during a campaign rally at the Freeman Coliseum on Oct. 7, 2026, in San Antonio, Texas. Trump was visiting the state to campaign for Republican candidates, including Senate candidate and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, ahead of the midterm elections. (Getty Images)

Bonds has never admitted to knowingly taking performance-enhancing drugs. The San Francisco Giants legend testified before a federal grand jury in 2003 that he unknowingly used a substance called "the clear," which is a designer anabolic steroid.

"The problem is he just looked like he took drugs," Trump said with a laugh.

"With Barry, it’s a little bit different (than Clemens) because there was very strong testimony and everything else," Trump said. "But I would consider. His numbers are so big, he was a great player and then he became a beyond great player."

Bonds' 762 home runs, 2,558 walks, 688 intentional walks and 162.8 bWAR are all MLB records. He was a seven-time MVP and a 14-time All-Star.

President Donald Trump (shakes hands with former MLB player Roger Clemens as he brings him on stage during a campaign rally at the Freeman Coliseum on Oct. 07, 2026, in San Antonio, Texas. On his third trip to the state in the last 30 days, Trump is visiting Texas to campaign for Republican candidates, including Senate candidate and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, ahead of the midterm elections. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Bonds received 66% of the vote in his final year on the ballot, short of the 75% required to earn induction.

Clemens peaked at 65.2% in his final year on the ballot. Unfortunately for him, he isn't eligible to be voted in again until 2031 because he received fewer than five votes from the 16-member Contemporary Baseball Era Committee in Dec. 2025. As a result, he became ineligible for the next three-year cycle under Hall of Fame rules. Bonds, who also received fewer than five votes from the committee, isn't eligible until 2031, either.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Sammy Kershaw responds to 'sellout' critics after attending 2026 CMA Awards red carpet
articles.excerpt: At the 2026 CMA Awards, Sammy Kershaw opens up about his private sit-down with the CMA, addressing critics who accused him of selling out and explaining why walking the red carpet meant ‘more than a c...
articles.body_text:
At the 2026 CMA Awards, Sammy Kershaw opens up about his private sit-down with the CMA, addressing critics who accused him of selling out and explaining why walking the red carpet meant ‘more than a carpet walk’ for country music fans.

Sammy Kershaw is addressing critics directly who suspect that he "sold out" for attending the 2026 Country Music Association awards.

Speaking to Fox News Digital on the red carpet, the legendary country music singer explained how he spoke with the association after taking to social media to air out his grievances about the association allegedly denying him and his wife access to walk the red carpet.

"Well, it went great, and I'm not going to tell you all the details of what was said. All I can tell you is that I know things were going in a positive direction. So, when we decided that I was going to come to the show and walk the carpet, there's a few people out there that said things like, 'Oh, he sold out' and this and that. But that's not how I look at it," Kershaw began.

ELLA LANGLEY DOMINATES CMA AWARDS WITH MAJOR WINS AS TAYLOR SWIFT MAKES STUNNING RETURN TO STAGE

Sammy Kershaw has responded to critics who believe he "sold out" by attending the 2026 CMA Awards. (Michael Buckner/Billboard via Getty Images)

"The way I look at it was, there was me and the CMA. And we came together and talked. We're moving in the right direction to a greater time in country music," Kershaw continued.

Without giving away details of the conversation, the country music star emphasized that both parties stayed for the whole conversation. "Nobody got up and walked away," he said.

Kershaw said that he didn't intend to hurt anyone with his Instagram post, but he was "heartbroken" by the association's decision.

"And then all of a sudden a lot of other people's fans came aboard. The fans, country music fans are country music fans, and they will bat for anybody in country music," Kershaw said. "Sometimes they'll get rough, but they came together for this because it was more than a carpet walk."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Sammy Kershaw and Mendy Kershaw attend the 60th Annual Country Music Association Awards. (Getty Images)

On Nov. 5, Kershaw uploaded a lengthy statement to Instagram, stating that the Country Music Association was not allowing him or his wife, Mendy, to walk the red carpet.

Kershaw claimed that he adjusted his tour schedule to accommodate this year's award show after being "strung along" for several months, assuming that they were invited.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"After more than 50 years in this business, many millions of records and singles streamed and sold, more than two dozen Billboard charted hits, a CMA Horizon Award nomination, being a lifetime CMA member, that they presented to me in 1992, and being asked to donate my time to play CMA Fest, I would hope I’ve earned the opportunity to walk the red carpet alongside my wife, as we’ve done before," Kershaw wrote.

Country musician Sammy Kershaw called out the CMAs on Instagram before the big night. (Getty Images)

He added, "I love country music, but never in a million years would I think that a successful country music entertainer (and I’m not the only one) would not be able to walk the red carpet. It’s extremely hurtful, embarrassing and very disappointing. I guess the next time I attend the CMA’s, it will be in tribute after I’m gone, if I’m lucky."

Country music stars poured into his comment section, supporting his message.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Sammy Kershaw and his wife, Mendy. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

Riley Duckman wrote, "If you haven’t earned the right to be there then nobody has… disappointing to say the least."

Granger Smith added: "So sad for country music. I grieve for the old CMA. … many of us wouldn’t be here without artists like you…"

Janelle Ash is an entertainment writer for Fox News Digital covering Hollywood, celebrity culture and breaking entertainment news through exclusive reporting, interviews and in-depth storytelling.

articles.title: Retired FBI agent warns NCIC breach could threaten police safety during traffic stops
articles.excerpt:
Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack breaks down what sits inside America’s law enforcement computers, how hackers get in and how to protect your data.

A retired FBI supervisory special a...
articles.body_text:
Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack breaks down what sits inside America’s law enforcement computers, how hackers get in and how to protect your data.

A retired FBI supervisory special agent warned Saturday that a cyber intrusion into the bureau's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) could endanger police officers during traffic stops if hackers altered records inside the database.

Jason Pack, a former FBI supervisory special agent who worked in cybercrime and public information, told Fox News Digital that the bureau's incident response team must quickly determine whether data was manipulated inside the system, which feeds criminal records to patrol cars nationwide.

"What they worry about is if any of this data has changed, then it might affect officers' safety on the side of the road," Pack said, noting there is no indication yet that any records were altered or that the system is experiencing an outage.

FBI PROBES SECOND CYBERATTACK IN MONTHS AS HACKERS BREACH KEY CRIME DATABASE, SOURCES SAY

Hackers have targeted the FBI for the second time in recent months. (Kevin Lamarque/Reuters, File)

Three sources familiar with the matter told Fox News that hackers breached the NCIC, marking the second cyberattack against the bureau in months. The FBI is investigating how the intruders gained entry and whether any information was compromised.

In an interview with Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany on Saturday morning, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the intrusion, adding, "I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that."

Pack described the NCIC as "America's computer for law enforcement," explaining that roughly 56 state terminals feed data out to hundreds of thousands of patrol car computers, so officers can check warrants, criminal histories, missing children, gang members and suspected terrorists.

FBI SAYS SOURCE OF ITS JOBS PORTAL BREACH STILL UNKNOWN AS HACKERS ALLEGE EMPLOYEE DATA COMPROMISED

While the database does not hold classified intelligence or sensitive FBI investigative case files, Pack said it stores personally identifiable information, including names, dates of birth and Social Security numbers.

Investigators will examine IP logs and metadata to determine whether attackers exploited a compromised password among the system's more than 100,000 users, breached a state terminal or infiltrated through a third-party vendor, Pack said, adding that cyberattacks have accelerated to "machine speed" as criminals increasingly use artificial intelligence to probe for vulnerabilities.

"You have this cat and mouse game where cybersecurity experts are trying to patch the vulnerabilities that they find. They're looking for their own vulnerabilities at the same time, they have to play defense against the criminals who are out there trying to steal information or do harm to our systems. I think we're just seeing now this speed of these intrusions ramp up a lot," Pack said.

TECH OUTAGE CASCADE EXPOSES US VULNERABILITIES TO FOREIGN CYBER THREATS

A cyber intrusion into the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) could endanger police officers during traffic stops, a retired agent says. (Getty Images, File)

The intrusion follows a September cyberattack in which the extortion group ShinyHunters breached an FBI job portal website and claimed to steal personal records belonging to bureau employees.

The latest incident also comes as a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report found 17 of 22 government agencies were not in compliance with federal cybersecurity regulations.

The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the NCIC breach.

Fox News Digital's James Cirrone and Greg Norman-Diamond, and Fox News' David Spunt contributed to this report.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Utah vs TCU prediction, odds and best bets: Utah faces a big time trap spot
articles.excerpt:
Devon Dampier found Creed Whittemore for a 70-yard game-winning TD to lift the Utah Utes over the Arizona Wildcats.

Utah has done everything right this season. The Utes are 10-0, No. 2 in the College...
articles.body_text:
Devon Dampier found Creed Whittemore for a 70-yard game-winning TD to lift the Utah Utes over the Arizona Wildcats.

Utah has done everything right this season. The Utes are 10-0, No. 2 in the College Football Playoff rankings and riding a 16-game winning streak dating to last season. They're in line for a first-round bye, and in Morgan Scalley's first year, they're the best story in the Big 12.

That's also why Saturday night in Fort Worth is a dangerous spot for the Utes.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Over the last two weeks, Utah has played two games that would drain any team. It beat rival BYU 28-20 in the Holy War, then had to rally for a 40-39 win at Arizona which was a bit of a letdown spot in its own right. Now the Utes are on the road again, for a 9:00 p.m. ET kickoff against a TCU team fighting for bowl eligibility, with one of the best defenses in the country, in what will surely be a rowdy atmosphere.

FIVE COLLEGE FOOTBALL BETS FOR SATURDAY, INCLUDING TWO ROAD DOGS THAT ARE BEING SLEPT ON

The market sees an unbeaten team against a .500 team. I see a letdown spot, a defense built to slow Utah down and a lot of bad luck about to turn around.

Utah -265 | TCU +215Spread: Utah -7.5 (-105) | TCU +7.5 (-115)Total: 46.5 (Over -110 / Under -110)

Saturday, Nov. 21, 9 p.m. ET, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth, FOX

This is about as lopsided as a betting market gets. Between 82% and 90% of the spread tickets are on Utah, and the Utes have drawn between 73% and 84% of the money.

The line has moved around with that action. Utah opened at -6.5, climbed as high as -7.5 and has settled between -7 and -7.5 depending on the book. The public is backing the undefeated team with the shiny ranking, and the books are happy to take it.

I love a classic contrarian spot, and in this one, I'm happy to go the other way.

WHAT IS A TEASER BET? HOW TEASERS WORK IN FOOTBALL AND BASKETBALL BETTING

Devon Dampier #4 of the Utah Utes and Ricky Johnson #11 of the Utah Utes celebrate after the touchdown during the second half against the Houston Cougars at Rice-Eccles Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. (Photo by Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) (Bryan Byerly/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Spots like this are where unbeaten teams lose.

Utah has been in close games almost every week since late September, and the last two were especially challenging. Winning a rivalry game against BYU and then rallying on the road at Arizona takes a lot out of a roster. This is the third straight week the Utes have played a meaningful, high-stress game, and it's another road trip with a late kickoff.

Don't get me wrong, I fully understand that Utah's offense is still dangerous. Devon Dampier has accounted for 31 touchdowns, 22 passing and nine rushing, and the Utes are scoring 37.9 points per game, 15th in the country. But this is the kind of game where good teams can look flat for a half, and against this defense, a flat half can be enough to put the Utes in trouble.

ESPN DISMISSES UTAH UTES AS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP CONTENDERS DESPITE BIG WIN OVER BYU: 'THEY WON'T WIN'

The TCU Horned Frog run onto the field for their season opener against UNC at Aer Aviva Stadium in Dublin, Ireland. (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Utah's offense isn't the only elite unit in this one. TCU's record hides how good its defense has been. The Horned Frogs allow just 15.2 points per game, 12th in the country, and they rank ninth nationally in net adjusted EPA per play allowed.

That's the matchup that matters. TCU has been at its best against offenses like Utah's. Under Sonny Dykes, the Horned Frogs are 17-7 straight up and 15-8-1 against the spread against teams averaging at least 425 yards per game. Dykes is also 6-3 against the spread as an underdog of 3.5 to 10 points, right in the range of this line.

This is the stat that makes the case, and I promise it's not a stretch. TCU has lost five games this season, and all five were decided by one score. Against Power 4 opponents, the Horned Frogs are 1-5 in one-score games, the most such losses of any Power 4 team. They've battled, but things have consistently gone against the Horned Frogs in close ones.

On the other side, Utah is 4-0 in those games. One could make the argument that good teams find a way to win those games, and that's true. But it's also true that there is some inherent luck in close games, and expecting that to always go your way i playing with fire.

Close-game records rarely hold over a full season. TCU hasn't been five losses worse than its opponents. It's been a handful of plays worse. Utah hasn't been four wins better, either. Eventually those coin flips start landing the other way, and a home game against a conference opponent with national championship aspirations is a good place for that to start for TCU.

WHAT IS A MONEYLINE BET? — HOW MONEYLINE ODDS, PAYOUTS AND FAVORITES WORK

A general view of the game between the TCU Horned Frogs and the Baylor Bears during the second half at Amon G. Carter Stadium on Oct. 18, 2025, in Fort Worth, Texas. (Getty Images)

It's only fair to make Utah's case too. The Utes are 8-2 against the spread and 7-1 as favorites of 6.5 or more. They score at an elite rate, and their defense allows only 18.6 points per game, 21st in the country.

TCU's offense is the real concern. The Horned Frogs score just 23.4 points per game, 103rd nationally, and they've been inconsistent all season. If Jaden Craig, who has thrown one interception over the last three games, can't move the ball, TCU's defense will eventually wear down.

That's why the points matter. I don't need TCU to outscore Utah. I need its defense to keep this within a score. If you're not a true believer in TCU at home, take the points.

This is the main play. Utah is in a letdown spot, the public is lopsided and TCU's defense is good enough to keep this close. The Horned Frogs have lost five games by a combined handful of plays. Getting more than a touchdown at home with that profile is the best number on the board.

If you believe in the letdown, take a smaller piece of the upset. At +215, the moneyline implies TCU wins about 32% of the time. With a top-12 scoring defense at home against a tired team on the road, that feels low.

The total fits the same story. TCU games have gone over just twice in 10 tries, and the Horned Frogs have averaged only 18.3 points per game in conference play. The early under action has been heavy, with every tracked ticket and dollar on the total backing the under.

If TCU's defense keeps Utah out of rhythm and its own offense grinds, this lands in the low 40s. That's the type of game where the underdog covers.

Utah is a great team, and it may still be a great futures bet to win the national title. But a 10-0 team playing its third straight high-stress game, on the road, late at night, against a top-12 defense with nothing to lose is how upsets happen.

Give me TCU +7.5 (-115), a sprinkle on the TCU moneyline (+215) and the under 46.5 (-110).

articles.title: Man found dead on Flinders Island linked to shooting of police officer, Tasmanian authorities say

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news pod...
articles.body_text:
Body of a man in his 20s discovered by police who were sent to investigate the shooting of an officer, who is in a serious but stable condition

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An on-duty police officer has been shot and a man found dead nearby as police investigate two firearm incidents in a tiny Tasmanian town.

The officer was working at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, north-east of the island of Tasmania, when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday night.

Police sent to investigate the shooting of the officer discovered the body of a man, believed to be in his mid-20s, with a gunshot wound on Walker Street, near the police station.

“At this time, police believe these two incidents are linked and that the situation has been safely contained,” Tasmanian police said in a statement on Sunday.

“Our thoughts are with the families and loved ones of those involved, and with the wider community of Flinders Island.”

The policeman is receiving treatment at the Royal Hobart hospital and remains in a serious but stable condition.

Whitemark has a population of about 300 according to the 2021 census, and the entire population of Flinders Island is fewer than 1,000 people.

Extra police resources, including forensic and uniformed officers, have been deployed to the island. Those with information about these incidents, including CCTV or dashcam footage of Walker Street, have been urged to contact police.

It is the second shooting of an on-duty police officer in Tasmania in 18 months. A Tasmanian officer was killed in the state’s north-west in June 2025 while executing a court-issued warrant to repossess a residence. The occupant of the home pleaded guilty to murder.

It is better to win ugly than to lose pretty, and BYU's season-saving triple-overtime win was not pretty.

No. 10 BYU (9-2) staved off Kansas (4-7) in a 31-29 thriller on Saturday afternoon at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. For a moment, it looked like the Cougars were going to come away with the win without requiring overtime.

Kansas tied the game at 16-16 with a touchdown with just over four minutes left in the game, but BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier led the Cougars into field goal range, leaving kicker Matthias Dunn a 37-yard field goal attempt with time expiring.

BYU wide receiver Jojo Phillips celebrates with teammates after scoring the game-winning touchdown in overtime of an NCAA college football game against Kansas on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Lawrence, Kan. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

However, instead of walking Kansas off in regulation, Dunn yanked the field goal attempt wide left as time expired, forcing overtime.

The Jayhawks got the ball first and quarterback Isaiah Marshall took the game over with his legs. On third-and-10, Marshall scrambled for 12 yards to keep the drive alive. BYU forced another third down, but Marshall again escaped the pocket and scored a touchdown, putting Kansas up 23-16 after the extra point.

It took BYU just three plays to respond, as a 23-yard pass from Bachmeier to wide receiver Kyler Kasper set up a 2-yard touchdown run from Bachmeier. After Dunn's extra point, the game was tied at 23-23.

Kansas quarterback Isaiah Marshall fumbles the ball under pressure from BYU safety Faletau Satuala during overtime of an NCAA college football game Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Lawrence, Kan. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

BYU got the ball first in the second overtime and scored in just four plays. Running back LJ Martin converted from 11 yards out, but in the second overtime, both teams must go for two if they score. Bachmeier's pass on the two-point conversion fell incomplete, meaning Kansas could win the game if it scored and converted on the two-point conversion.

BYU's defense was on the brink of closing the game out, as it forced a fourth-and-5 on Kansas' opening series. However, Marshall threw up a prayer to the end zone as he was being pressured, and wide receiver Nahzae Cox went up and hauled it in for a 20-yard touchdown to tie the game 29-29.

Kansas squandered its opportunity to pull off the upset when Marshall was pressured in the pocket and threw the pass over the end zone.

BYU running back LJ Martin celebrates after scoring a touchdown during overtime of an NCAA college football game against Kansas on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Lawrence, Kan. (AP Photo/Charlie Riedel)

In the third overtime, only two-point conversions can be attempted, and the Jayhawks went first. Marshall again found himself under pressure and was stripped of the ball in the pocket.

BYU, afforded an opportunity to walk off Kansas for a second time, capitalized in triple overtime. Bachmeier found Jojo Phillips in the end zone for the two-point conversion, sealing the win.

The roller coaster win saved the Cougars' College Football Playoff dreams. They will have to beat Cincinnati at home next week to strengthen their case to be in the tournament.

articles.title: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
articles.excerpt:
George Washington died in 1799 after serving for two terms as America's first president

A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (£...
articles.body_text:
George Washington died in 1799 after serving for two terms as America's first president

A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (£3,058).

The hair once belonged to John Gadsby, who entertained Washington in 1799 just before the latter's death the same year, and was later obtained by a collector called John K Lattimer from a descendent of Gadsby's, according to Richmond Auctions, which sold the item.

Saturday's sale is not the most expensive for Washington hair at auction. Three strands thought to have been removed from him close to or after his death stored in a locket sold for nearly $40,000 in 2021.

Gadsby, a resident of what in 1799 was the town of Alexandria in Virginia, entertained Washington for dinner shortly before his death later that year, according to a testament given in 1928 by Gadsby's granddaughter, Julia Ten Eyck McBlair, and which was posted on the Richmond Auctions website.

McBlair stated that her grandfather came into possession of Washington's hair "in view of the friendship and association with his last days" and had it framed and hung "under General Washington's portrait in our home in Washington City, there I have seen it all my life".

Gadsby hosted Washington's two birthday celebrations in 1798 and 1799, Richmond Auctions states.

Washington led American forces to victory against the British in the War of Independence and helped draft the US Constitution before becoming the country's first president in 1788. He stepped down in 1797 after serving two terms.

Several locks of Washington's hair have been preserved, including at least 50 examples that are in a collection at his former residence, Mount Vernon, which is now a museum.

"Public displays of hair from friends or loved ones peaked in the 19th century, but had long been popular among affluent families like the Washingtons," a blog on the Mount Vernon website states.

As well as lockets of his hair, other items associated with Washington have also done well at auction.

In July, a signed letter by Washington from 1776, in which he asks for soldiers for the Continental Army to fight the British, sold for $109,800.
